📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • PC Gamer's got your back Our experienced team dedicates many hours to every review, to really get to the heart of what matters most to you.
  • World of Warcraft: Forever has, much as the original World of Warcraft did back in 2004, completely consumed my life.
  • Sources indicate that what is it?: A reimagining of 2004's World of Warcraft, with new balancing, lighting, dungeons, and items.Expect to pay: A monthly subscription of $14.99/£10.99.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A hopeful rebirth for the old-school MMO formula.

PC Gamer's got your back Our experienced team dedicates many hours to every review, to really get to the heart of what matters most to you. Find out more about how we evaluate games and hardware.

World of Warcraft: Forever has, much as the original World of Warcraft did back in 2004, completely consumed my life. I write about games for a living, mind, so the attention vortex it has wrought upon me is primarily professional obligation, rather than just irresponsibility.

Sources indicate that what is it?: A reimagining of 2004's World of Warcraft, with new balancing, lighting, dungeons, and items.Expect to pay: A monthly subscription of $14.99/£10.99. Optional race and early-game zone behind a £25.99/$30 paywall.Developer: Blizzard EntertainmentPublisher: Blizzard EntertainmentReviewed on: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060, AMD Ryzen 7 5800 8-Core Processor, 16GB RAM, Force MP600 SSDMultiplayer?: YesLink: Official site.

According to recent reports, but at the time of writing, it has been 443 hours since Forever's launch. I have spent 147 of those hours asleep (less, but let's just pretend I've been getting a solid eight), leaving around 296 hours of my waking mind. 230 of them have been spent playing World of Warcraft.

That's a deeply concerning amount of time if I wasn't getting a salary to review it—it has been part of my 9-5. I've also often been keeping the game open while I, you know, feed and bathe myself and do chores. So we're probably just in the realm of 'moderately worrying' rather than 'cause for a wellness check'.

Recent findings suggest that don't worry, I intend to take a break soon: But during those 230 hours, I have hit level 60, entered 31 dungeons, completed 941 quests, levelled engineering, mining, and first aid to 300, and apparently /waved at other players 50 times. Which are rookie numbers that I need to get up.

But I've also found myself taking in the scenery, laughing at my poor luck at bottles, whining about the drop rates of basilisk brains, splitting mining nodes with party members, mercilessly grinding ogres into paste for my first mount, and talking to more strangers while questing than I have in years of playing more modern, streamlined MMOs.

Recent findings suggest that I'm not pointing this out to simply cast aside the role of nostalgia in my enjoyment, but I do think nostalgia can only carry an attention span so far. It certainly doesn't keep 230 hours of medically inadvisable gameplay afloat on its own. There's something else going on here; something special that's been unearthed.

All of the things that made an old-school MMO like the original WoW so deeply enthralling back in 2004 are not simply dated, to be cast aside as an inferior form of videogame.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

The crappy drop rates, the fighting over tags, the running everywhere (there is so much running everywhere) while not always justified, is part of an experience that's stronger for its inconveniences. The friction burn you get from jutting up against a game that's occasionally just hostile to you. All of that connects you to the world, and the people in it, in a very real way.

Sources indicate that first, I want to talk about what Forever itself has actually brought to the table. After all, much of what I've talked about already has been reverence paid to a series of design decisions that were made over 20 years ago.

In the here and now, though, Forever has around 1,000 upcoming quests (the original WoW is estimated to've had somewhere in the mid-2,000s, so that's approximately 30-50% more Warcraft), nine new dungeons, and two new major levelling zones in Mount Hyjal and The Riverglades.

To encourage and support levelling alts, Blizzard's added a new mechanic in the Legacy tree—a genuinely cool feature that encourages you to level alts (or do endgame achievements and raids) to unlock perks, like making levelling slightly easier by giving you a small heal when you kill an enemy in the open world, or by giving you more resources when you gather things.

According to recent reports, then there's the retooled class and item balance, the latter of which is my one, very mild point of disappointment: There's an increasing amount of trinkets and weapons I've kept around for specific use cases, sure, but at least while levelling, the fantasy of equipping an anti-worgen sword to do some worgen-killing quests (as so often quoted in Blizzard's promotional material) hasn't quite panned out. That's not to say it's gone by the wayside completely, though.

It has been revealed that I've seen a two-handed axe that lets you get mining nodes, a knife that lets you skin humanoids, gloves that increase your mining skill, boots that let you walk under water, and so on. It's just not a core part of the levelling experience.

In a recent development, it does also improve somewhat when you get into the later levels. For instance, I now have a two-handed questing sword green that I'll keep in my bags basically forever because it lets me spin around like a propeller to slow my fall speed: And I'm a Warrior, so that's a hugely useful traversal tool for someone without any way to slow fall.

Professions have also had a total facelift, and for the first time, I'm actually levelling crafting and gathering skills on my characters because of it.

Not only do crafting ones like blacksmithing actually give you really good gear as you level up (rather than just a couple of big capstone items) but all professions can now turn in writs and crates, buying new recipes via the latter and unlocking them with a rep grind via the former.

Industry observers note that the new zones are both excellent—the Riverglades is pretty, but not out of place, whereas Hyjal is a satisfying (and very efficient) climb up a mythological mountain ruined by war, with some legitimately cool questlines to it. In both, questing is enough of a breeze that it does feel almost too easy, with Hyjal smoothing over the typically arduous 58-60 grind completely. But they're not any more efficient than, say, The Burning Crusade's better zones, which is a level of kayfabe-breaking I can get behind.

Recent findings suggest that but until you hit that point, Forever's newness is downright subtle. A chain here, a few fetch quests there. Just enough to make questing in every zone worth it, just enough to even out the occasional, clunky speedbumps.

Recent findings suggest that with Riverglades being level 38, and Mount Hyjal not mattering until the final stretch, Forever partially buries the lede, and you'd be forgiven for thinking it a touch unambitious. But with Blizzard's commitment to add new Riverglade-style zones and questlines to the game in the years to come, it's going to keep morphing into something new with the passing years, and what's there—when you get to it—is plainly impressive.

It has been revealed that such as Forever's upcoming dungeons. I've done seven out of the new nine crawls, and while they're a little more mechanically dense than the vanilla predecessors (bosses sometimes have like, two moves) I've been fascinated by just how well that old-school design has been emulated.

In a recent development, with the exception of Alcaz Island, these things are sprawling, time-consuming romps. And, while controversial, the changes to dungeon XP (putting the majority of it in their quests while lowering the amount you get from mobs) has made completing them an adventure.

I recently knocked out Sunken Temple's questline, but the world-trotting, multiple quest-chain journey to get all my pre-requisites had me doing another unrelated dungeon a second time, fighting my way to the top of a troll fortress in the Hinterlands, helping out a drunk dwarf, and speaking to the spirit of a fallen Horde warrior to get his hipflask.

Recent findings suggest that so when it was time to finally darken the door of the Sunken Temple and get it all done, I felt accomplished. Like I'd not just rocked up to a portal to get some fat loots, but that I'd actually—like an adventurer might—spent considerable time researching, preparing, and bracing myself for the place.

Didn't stop us forgetting that the Shade of Eranikus summons all the right now-alive dragon adds to him and getting absolutely mauled, but hey-ho.

More to the point, my XP reward for that journey felt considerably far more potent than if I'd simply hopped in there to rinse it 5 times. And I might have skipped it if the XP reward wasn't mostly dispensed via questing. I won't say dungeon XP isn't an issue for some players, but for me, the exercise works.

There hasn't just been an RTX-on style filter slapped over Azeroth, this is all bespoke.".

And while you're running around the world, forced to jog ignobly between major locations, Forever's upcoming lighting system and draw distance shines through. The reason these lighting changes aren't in retail yet is because, primarily, they're hand-crafted.

Durotar has these darling oversaturated blue shadows, Felwood bathes everything in a sickly green, Duskwood's mist hangs thick in the air, and the lightning that crackles over the Blasted Lands actually casts electric blue light across the stones of Nethergarde Keep.

But there are subtle changes, too. You can see Nordrassil, the world tree at the top of Mount Hyjal, from Durotar—as well as other zones on the continent. Dun Morogh and Winterspring have uniquely hostile snowstorm blizzards that cut out visibility entirely, similar to Tanaris' sandstorms.

Recent findings suggest that there hasn't just been an RTX-on style filter slapped over Azeroth, this is all bespoke, and it's made all of my journeys that much more atmospheric. I've had to stop just to take in the godrays pushing through the canopy of Ashenvale, or the burning sunset descending on the seas of Stormwind Harbor.

Industry observers note that more importantly, these effects really pull out the strengths of that old-school mode of design. Both the 2004 version of World of Warcraft and Forever understand that in order for a world to feel massive, it needs to be difficult to traverse sometimes. In order for it to be social, there needs to be a level of unfairness that being social will overcome.

I thoroughly enjoyed World of Warcraft: Midnight, the latest expansion in modern World of Warcraft, when I reviewed it for launch. I thought the questlines, which I can remember the glossy cinematics and major storybeats of, were engaging enough. And I still think its newly introduced revamped Silvermoon is gorgeous, and a complete flex from the studio's art team.

I could not, however, tell you a single thing about my questing experience that wasn't dictated to me by the game. Yes, I liked certain story beats or character conversations, but the actual experience of hitting stuff? It's a blur. I flew somewhere, I pushed my buttons, I interacted with something. I flew somewhere else, and you know what I did there? I pushed more buttons.

In contrast, I've been playing Forever for almost three weeks, and I've already made memories. On a jog to an annoying Scarlet Monastery dungeon questline that sent me to Desolace, I met up with two dwarven brothers (or husbands? They had the same second name) who were making the journey. We joined up with more people to kill a bunch of high-level skeletons, and barely got through an overpull by the skin of our teeth.

In Stranglethorn Vale, a kindly shadow priest six levels higher than me partied up to kill some pirates, then pointed out that there was a good questline that could be done by scavenging beach bottles. They got theirs on their first try. I, for some reason, had to pick up 26 of the damn things.

On another journey, I decided to try and grab my fire-hardened mail armor for a warrior questline, which sent my alliance character all the way into The Barrens, to Razorfen Kraul. This is not a great dungeon to do if you're an alliance character, so the pickings were slim. Which meant that I not only tanked the whole thing as Fury, but that the folks I was with were chill enough to do a quick road-trip to Feralas with me to get another dungeon quest.

Sources indicate that the point being, I only had these memorable experiences and spoke to these people because I was being, and I know this is a bad word for a lot of MMO players, inefficient. Absolute bastard questlines made me do something far out of the way. And every single time I've played along, I wound up having a lovely time meeting similarly stubborn folks and making fresh friends.

A lot of these inconveniences, carried over from vanilla and left alone in Forever, are there to push you and people you meet organically, out in the world, into close quarters and camaraderie. To do "kill X" quests, you need to intentionally party up with that random night elf warrior, rather than just pass them by. To get certain questlines accomplished at the level they're given, you need to ask for help in general chat.

Some chains will send you to some random city, forcing you to learn the most efficient boat route to get there—or to simply leave that quest in your log until you next happen to pop your head into Darnassus. The travel time makes the world feel big. The encouraged cooperation makes it feel alive and social. And all that friction produces friendships—these quests suck to do on your own but are so often a breeze to do together. Or, at the very least, they're more entertaining with manufacturer.

This is why it doesn't just feel like nostalgia to me. It's the rub of the whole thing. I am not enjoying these quests because, at some time in the past, I had a nice innocent memory surrounding them that I'm reliving. It's actually all about what's happening in the present: Grouping up with people, striking up conversations, sharing in misery as it takes a full 45 minutes to fill our bags with pirate hats.

In a recent development, I'm honestly just marvelling about the fact that, in 2026, that this sort of design still works. It works tremendously well. Blizzard's new campfire mechanic, which I like a lot, is just a cherry-on-top-nudge towards striking up the conversations I was already having anyway.

So many times, my purposefully chill vibes have been met with genuine kindness: People stay on to help you finish quests they've already completed, they show you latest questlines. Sometimes it's a tit-for-tat. A shaman helped me out with my level 50 warrior quest in exchange for me helping him kill an elite somewhere, which hey, fair dos.

This all culminated in an incident where I joined in for a random kill quest in my mid-40s. A priest, around their mid-40s as well, commented that man, a lotta folks had their mounts already! Myself included. I'd spent a few hours mining over 200 Iron Ores and killing cave ogres, like a maniac.

Industry observers note that I asked how far off they were. They stated they had 80 gold out of 90. I threw 15 gold at them before I realised what I was doing.

Sources indicate that this isn't to humblebrag, mind. My grinding had produced a surplus of cash that I wasn't really spending: But it was like I'd been suddenly possessed by the spirit of Christmases past, future, and present. I gave a complete stranger a significant amount of money with the complete understanding I'd never talk to them again. Because I felt like being nice, because so many people had been nice to me.

Sources indicate that I do understand the yearning for flight paths, for lower respec costs, for shared mob tagging, and for quests that don't require your character to walk the circumference of the earth. And if none of that's to your taste, then hey, fine—but more than anything, Forever's proven to me that those flying mount doomers back in The Burning Crusade might've been onto something.

In a recent development, I still enjoy 'theme park' MMOs, but Forever is such a deeply exciting prospect to me. It's a second chance for this older, slower, more social form of videogame to have a renaissance. Before booting up Forever on November 4, I couldn't tell you the last time I had an adventure (an organic one, not one delivered to me through a storyline) in an MMORPG. Two weeks later, and I've had several, and I keep logging on and embarking on these long, arduous quest chains because I'm excited to have more.

In a recent development, forever is such rare air. A major MMO studio has been given the blessing to revamp a 20+ year old version of a game and add to it. And while it's already added a considerable amount, Forever feels like proof that, given enough exposure in the spotlight, people could actually like a newly introduced MMO with its design sensibilities.

And as a fan of lots of different kinds of MMOs—be they slow-paced adventures like Forever or on-rails dungeon-rinsing theme parks like Final Fantasy 14—I want this genre to have the kind of actual diversity it deserves. More MMOs than World of Warcraft should get to take this sort of risk. More MMOs should be able to take it slow.

Until that new game comes, however, I'll happily play Forever, and I cannot wait to roll up an alt to start doing it all over again.

A hopeful rebirth for the old-school MMO formula.

In a recent development, harvey's history with games started when he first begged his parents for a World of Warcraft subscription aged 12, though he's since been cursed with Final Fantasy 14-brain and a huge crush on G'raha Tia. He made his start as a freelancer, writing for websites like Techradar, The Escapist, Dicebreaker, The Gamer, Into the Spine—and of course, PC Gamer. He'll sink his teeth into anything that looks interesting, though he has a soft spot for RPGs, soulslikes, roguelikes, deckbuilders, MMOs, and weird indie titles. He also plays a shelf load of TTRPGs in his offline time. Don't ask him what his favourite system is, he has too many.

GTA 6's strong and silent Jason was inspired by Steve McQueen and former Army Rangers, says Rockstar

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Speaking to Destructoid over email, Rockstar's senior vice president of narrative, Rupert Humphries, explained that the team looked at classic couple-on-the-run films when it decided on GTA 6's story.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you've noticed that Grand Theft Auto 6's Jason Duval isn't much of a talker, that's by design, as his quiet nature was inspired by Steve McQueen and the studio's research into former Army Rangers.

Speaking to Destructoid over email, Rockstar's senior vice president of narrative, Rupert Humphries, explained that the team looked at classic couple-on-the-run films when it decided on GTA 6's story.

"When we decided we wanted to tell a story about a couple on the run, we looked at all the similar kinds of movies, and one of the ones that really stood out was Peckinpah's The Getaway," Humphries said. "Steve McQueen was famous for pulling lines out of scripts and saying things with his presence alone. We wanted to see how close we could get to that with a game character, where so many of our protagonists have been the opposite.".

That approach also fitted the studio's research into veterans. "This also resonated with the research we were doing around veterans and particularly former Army Rangers (in our world we call them Marauders)," Humphries continued. "These guys typically aren't running their mouths or reacting to something unless it's strictly necessary, while still being strong and still asserting themselves.".

Game writer Michael Wiafe said Florida's real-life crime stories were "an obvious starting point" for GTA 6's characters more broadly.

"From then on, it was about coming up with authentic characters that didn't stray too far from reality but also were not totally bound by it either," Wiafe said. "The majority of our main characters are undeniably reprehensible on paper, full-blown criminals, but also decent human beings. Their moral makeup isn't necessarily cut-and-dry, and we don't attempt to make excuses for them.".

Industry observers note that fellow writer Elizabeth Gauvey-Kern added that while "the story takes some pretty heavy turns", Jason and Lucia's goal remains consistent. "So sharing their sense of determination, the focus on their goal, through all the highs and lows - that's what I hope people feel more than anything. You really want them to make it.".

GTA 6 introduced on Thursday, 19th November, for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S, and while it's the biggest entertainment launch of all time, selling 32.5 million pre-release copies and making $3.79 billion by the end of its first day, not everyone is happy: some players have been review bombing its Metacritic user score over its limited FPS and purported "woke" agenda.

Eurogamer called GTA 6 an open world of "awe, minute detail and impossible scale" in our five-star GTA 6 review. If you need help getting through the game now that it's here, you can check out Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough and a breakdown of our Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

Just don't share any, uh, spicy in-game screenshots via PSN - we recently learned that a GTA 6 player was hit with a 30-day PlayStation Network ban after sending a friend a photo they took in the game's nudist resort.

Activision patents AI voice system that learns from in-game chat and creates audio for NPCs who can even speak in place of you

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (415 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, call of Duty publisher Activision has filed for a upcoming patent allowing it to train NPCs on real-world player voice chat.
  • It has been revealed that the patent, spotted by Patentlyze, was filed in July and published in November.
  • The system compares those captured player reactions and then correlates them with coinciding gameplay events in order to understand their significance, essentially learning as it goes what triggers certain reactions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, call of Duty publisher Activision has filed for a upcoming patent allowing it to train NPCs on real-world player voice chat. The patent describes an AI-driven system that listens in on player voice chat following key gameplay moments and later recreates it using in-game characters.

It has been revealed that the patent, spotted by Patentlyze, was filed in July and published in November. According to the filing and its diagrams, the system is a self-learning neural network that recognises major gameplay moments - such as kills, longshots, deaths and so on - and records the player's reaction and voice chat from the moment just before and then after they happen. These can be as simple as brief celebratory shouts, groans or yells, or as complex as trash talk.

The system compares those captured player reactions and then correlates them with coinciding gameplay events in order to understand their significance, essentially learning as it goes what triggers certain reactions. The AI then teaches itself to quickly identify those when they occur in-game and replicate them.

Sources indicate that although the replicated voice lines don't directly repeat players' own chat, the system does keep a profile of each player it analyses so it can deliver a response tailored to them, including sticking to the same spoken language, which it uses large language models (LLMs) to help identify. The patent describes a filter of sorts to keep NPCs from learning offensive language such as slurs.

According to the patent, the system's reach extends beyond in-game voice chat to also potentially access voice comms from major apps like Discord.

Activision's goal is to create NPCs that can speak naturally, rather than re-use the same pre-recorded lines. The application seems to be limited to multiplayer games, including those with co-op. Think of the generic voice lines spoken by AI-teammates like "cover me" and so on in a PvE game, or the many other similar ones in battle royale and PvP matches that contain dozens or hundreds of players.

Incidentally, the patent talks of replacing those generic messages with learned ones for players who join a match without a microphone, but players can also seemingly allow their in-game avatars to always use generated voices.

As the game industry continues to grapple with the use of generative-AI in game development, Activision's patent seems to be going directly to source, recreating how those LLMs and AI systems got their knowledge to begin with: from humans.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that rocky has returned to the significant screen amid the 2026 movie schedule, but not in the way fans of the fictional boxer would’ve likely expected.
  • As awards season heats up, the cast and creative team behind I Play Rocky have been making the rounds and promoting the movie.
  • So, after he signed off, I mentioned — we had the discussion [of] should he come on as a producer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that rocky has returned to the significant screen amid the 2026 movie schedule, but not in the way fans of the fictional boxer would’ve likely expected. Sylvester Stallone’s journey to getting the iconic 1976 film made is chronicled in the acclaimed biopic, I Play Rocky, which is helmed by Peter Farrelly. While Stallone had no direct involvement in the movie, he did give it his official stamp of approval to the creative team. However, the beloved actor accidentally sparked some serious drama after the movie was unveiled, and I was totally unaware of it.

As awards season heats up, the cast and creative team behind I Play Rocky have been making the rounds and promoting the movie. Farrelly recently took part in a wide-ranging discussion with Deadline as part of its Contenders series and reflected on making his latest flick. During the discussion, the Dumb and Dumber helmer spoke about receiving input from Stallone early on about his approach to his family, including his father, Frank Stallone Sr. Also, Sly and Farrelly agreed on a key detail that led the latter to make a request:.

There’s a funny story. So, after he signed off, I mentioned — we had the discussion [of] should he come on as a producer. I said, ‘Personally, I think you should not. I think it’s going to hurt you. Because you come across so great [in the film] and, at the end of the movie, if they see ‘executive-produced by Sylvester Stallone’ they’re going to think you shaped it,’ which he didn’t. And he agreed with that, and I said, ‘Just separate yourself a little from this.’.

Honestly, the Oscar-winning filmmaker’s rationale (as shared on X) makes a lot of sense. If Stallone were credited as a producer on the film, which shows him in a mostly positive light, many may be tempted to think he manipulated the narrative. The Rambo star is, of course, no stranger to moviemaking so, given his directing and producing experience, I can see why he’d agree. Despite coming to an accord on Stallone needing to “separate” himself from the production, that apparently led to a serious faux pas on the actor’s part:.

In a recent development, A week later, he’s doing an interview, and a guy claims, ‘What do you think about this movie about the making of Rocky?’ And he goes, ‘I know nothing about it.’ And the internet goes crazy…. [People are like,] ‘These motherfuckers, they’re doing this movie without even going to Sylvester Stallone. Frank Stallone is threatening our lives, [Sly’s] brother. And Frank is like, ‘Can you believe these blah blah blah blah blah.’.

Sources indicate that the mere thought of getting heat from fans is daunting enough, but receiving heat from a member of the Stallone family is something else entirely. Farrelly went on to say that he later had another chat with the purveyor and lover of the Rocky films, and it went down as follows:.

I called Sylvester [and] I go, ‘What are you doing?!’ He goes, ‘What?’ I stated, ‘You said you knew nothing about it.’ He goes, ‘You said to separate myself.’ [I said,] ‘Not that far.’ And he indicates, ‘Oh okay, I will remember that going forward.’.

It has been revealed that I Thought Rocky And Creed's Significant Fight Scene Would Be The End Of I Play Rocky. So What Happened?

Sources indicate that while all this drama was due to a simple misunderstanding, it definitely created quite a mess for the filmmaking team. No lasting damage was seemingly done, though, and I’d say that things have been working out for Farrelly and his collaborators. The movie has been well received and gaining considerable buzz in the lead-up to the Oscars. It even received a stamp of approval from Ryan Gosling. As for Stallone, he admitted he was prepared to be “hypercritical” of the film, but he ended up really enjoying the movie as a whole and lead actor Anthony Ippolito’s portrayal of him.

I’d say that’s a generally happy ending to this story in the aftermath of the unintentional drama. Something I appreciate, though, is that Peter Farrelly is far enough removed from the situation that he can joke about it now. What isn’t a laughing matter, though, is the amount of heart that’s present in I Play Rocky, and fans can check out the film in theaters now.

60 hours in GTA 6 has me yearning for an online Leonida

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (863 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pcgamer

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that I honestly can't recall the last time I took such delight in existing within a virtual world as the way I have with Grand Theft Auto 6's Leonida.
  • Industry observers note that pockets of culture erupt all over: the sheer redneckery of Port Gellhorn, the Latin culture that permeates Little Cuba, and the affluent snootiness of Capri that has cops flinging microaggressions in every direction.
  • Recent findings suggest that it's a world that, when I first ventured into it, I had no interest in exploring in a multiplayer setting.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that I honestly can't recall the last time I took such delight in existing within a virtual world as the way I have with Grand Theft Auto 6's Leonida. Rockstar has delivered on its promise of both breadth and depth—the map is huge, but utterly stuffed with detail. Large, open highways shrink into single lanes surrounded by construction that force me to slam the brakes. Sidewalks sparse with pedestrians eventually lead to densely packed retail areas, restaurants, and clubs.

Industry observers note that pockets of culture erupt all over: the sheer redneckery of Port Gellhorn, the Latin culture that permeates Little Cuba, and the affluent snootiness of Capri that has cops flinging microaggressions in every direction. You don't need to undertake any missions in these areas to understand the people that live here—Rockstar has nailed so much of the environmental storytelling and the conversations between NPCs you'll stumble on as you roam.

Recent findings suggest that it's a world that, when I first ventured into it, I had no interest in exploring in a multiplayer setting. I spent an ungodly amount of time in GTA 5's Online mode when it first released. I was there on the ground for its incredibly shaky launch (I made a character and then got stuck in that birdseye view loading screen for hours, incredible stuff) and continued to sink time into it over the years, particularly during Covid.

And I like it well enough, but its novelty has waned over the last decade. Its core experience is inherently different from what singleplayer brings, and I had yearned to return to a world less about blowing other players up with flying motorbikes and more about, well, blowing non-players up with regular motorbikes.

But after 60 hours roaming around Leonida and witnessing what it has to offer? I now want nothing more than for Rockstar to spin this map into the next generation of Online. Even outside of missions and driving around, there are so many little things that I would kill to do with pals.

Recent findings suggest that grab a pack of brewskis from the convenience store, hop in a boat, and go fishing. Throw on our best all-American attire and get down and dirty in some mud racing. Seek out other players meticulously planning a jewellery store hold-up, only to swoop in and steal the goods for ourselves. Hit up the gym for a little workout before nipping to a nearby restaurant for a bite to eat. Leonida is a place that is so rife with things to do, and I can imagine doing almost all of them with some buddies by my side.

Industry observers note that it's also the perfect opportunity for Rockstar to introduce things that are sorely missing for me right now. A lack of safehouses makes sense with GTA 6's offline story, but I yearn to buy highrise apartments and suburban houses. Maybe even buy a business or two, for a little side cash. There's also the matter of that gigantic casino and the go-kart track that are currently inaccessible but the latter of which is donning a large "COMING SOON" sign. It feels like I'm being taunted. Surely you wouldn't put these things in the game with no intention of opening them at some point… right?

Keep up to date with the most crucial stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Industry observers note that and even as someone who was never interested in nor dabbled with GTA Online's flourishing roleplaying scene, I've encountered so many instances where I've thought roleplaying in Leonida actually be pretty darn neat. I could become a RydeMe driver, or a Snapmatic influencer, or a backwater recluse who lives off the land. And when the game comes to PC? The potential for bending the world to account for even more professions becomes all the greater.

It has been revealed that rockstar hasn't actually said a damn thing about GTA 6 Online right now, but it feels inevitable. Leonida is the biggest playground the developer has given players to date, and unleashing players across its sprawling map is Online's natural evolution. And, y'know, considering how much money GTAO has made over the last 13 years, I'm almost certain that Rockstar won't leave that kind of opportunity on the table.

Why Kate Middleton's Return to William's Side Says a Lot About the Future of the Monarchy

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1857 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vanityfair

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that after days of rumors circulating about Kate Middleton’s possible participation in the trip to India, confirmation came only at the last minute.
  • The Prince and Princess of Wales arrive at the Earthshot ceremony.
  • In a recent development, kate’s participation in the royal tour was made official by Kensington Palace only the day before departure to allow the princess to assess her condition right up until the last minute and determine whether she could handle such a demanding trip, following her recovery.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that after days of rumors circulating about Kate Middleton’s possible participation in the trip to India, confirmation came only at the last minute. This news came as a surprise in many ways, even though the princess’s presence was expected. Her involvement in this tour of India deserves attention, especially in light of the increasingly vital role she plays alongside Prince William, who will be king. The trip to India, significant in its own right, also included an important meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, aimed at strengthening relations between the United Kingdom and India. This high-profile diplomatic meeting was added after it was confirmed that Modi would return in time from his trip to the Philippines.

The Prince and Princess of Wales arrive at the Earthshot ceremony.

In a recent development, kate’s participation in the royal tour was made official by Kensington Palace only the day before departure to allow the princess to assess her condition right up until the last minute and determine whether she could handle such a demanding trip, following her recovery. But once she arrived in Mumbai, Catherine proved she was ready to do more than initially planned. The princess appeared, as always, impeccable and smiling—perhaps even more so than usual—in her customary understated and polished style. She greeted the crowd and met with people who had come to see her, participating in events alongside her husband.

Industry observers note that from the first day of this three-day tour—which began on the anniversary of their official engagement— Kate immediately displayed her characteristic good-natured spirit, evident in past tours as well, by joining Prince William in a game of gully cricket—a street version of the sport—alongside local children and teenagers. Serving as host was Sachin Tendulkar, an Indian sports legend whom the couple had already met during their previous visit to the country in 2016. The two princes put their skills to the test with little formality. They then took a ride on the Mumbai metro—a scene we’d already seen in London in candid photos when the Princess of Wales traveled on a bus in celebration of London Poppy Day.

The Princess of Wales at the awards ceremony.

The highlight was the awards ceremony in Mumbai on the evening of the second day, when the Princess of Wales unexpectedly took the stage to deliver a speech dedicated to the power of nature, health, and healing. Her speech was kept secret until the last moment, so much so that not even the celebrities and other guests in attendance knew the Princess of Wales would be speaking. “Nature is precious,” the princess stated. “We are not separate from it. We are part of it, deeply connected in ways both visible and unseen…the health of the planet and our natural world is inseparable from our own, and when it thrives, so do we,” she continued. “I have seen firsthand how nature has the power to heal and enrich our daily lives, but so much remains under threat.” “There will be good days and bad days, that it will take time.".

Sources indicate that catherine then presented the award in the “Protect and Restore Nature” category, dedicated to the protection and restoration of ecosystems. “The people we’re celebrating tonight are a huge part of that story. Their work will inspire and create seismic change that will improve lives for generations to come,” she stated.

The Prince and Princess of Wales at the awards ceremony.

It has been revealed that over the past three days, William and Kate have been busy meeting about sustainability, innovation, transportation, culture, and relations between the two countries. William is, in fact, assuming an increasingly prominent role on the international stage, supporting the United Kingdom’s diplomatic relations through his travels, which Middleton’s presence reinforced. This time, however, it was not simply a princess accompanying her husband on an official visit, but a woman who, after her illness and a long hiatus from major trips abroad, chose to return to her rightful role—and one the public has long expected her to fill.

The Prince and Princess of Wales with some Earthshot Prize winners.

It’s worth noting that this is the first time in four years—since her illness—that Kate has accompanied Prince William on an official overseas mission. The last such occasion was in December 2022, when the couple traveled to Boston, Massachusetts, for the Earthshot Prize ceremony. Her participation in the trip to India thus reflects her desire to gradually resume her international role, as well as her awareness of just how vital her presence is to the monarchy.

After her cancer diagnosis in 2024, Catherine prioritized her health and family, returning to public engagements without rushing things. However, her trip to Reggio Emilia, Italy, last May marked an key first step. On that occasion, she appeared visibly engaged and enthusiastic, and in subsequent statements, she hinted at her desire to travel more and gradually resume international engagements. “So I’m so glad it went well for her. I think she came back buzzing.” William said, describing his wife’s mood after that trip. Court circles had also hinted that Catherine wished to gradually resume a more active schedule.

The Prince and Princess of Wales at the 2026 Earthshot Prize ceremony.

In a recent development, her return to work, however, was approached gradually, respecting the time needed for her recovery. It’s a journey that Kate herself described with great sincerity in a recent interview published last week in Country Life, a magazine for which Prince William served as guest editor. “I was told in hospital that my recovery would not be linear. There will be good days and bad days, that it will take time,” the princess noted, emphasizing that recovery does not necessarily proceed in a steady and predictable manner. India, therefore, did not come as a complete surprise. Rather, it was the realization of a desire that Middleton had already begun to express, and that the princess agreed to undertake such a demanding trip indicates she felt ready to take the next step.

The Prince and Princess of Wales in India.

Before the trip, Kensington Palace issued a statement emphasizing how much the princess cares about her husband’s environmental initiative and how meaningful it was for her to return to participate in the ceremony in person. “She’s enormously proud of what he’s achieved, and it has been particularly special for them to experience this moment together. They are very much a team.”.

This refers to the project’s growth; since her last participation in Boston in 2022, it has significantly expanded its international reach and the impact of the initiatives it supports. “This year’s program in Mumbai promises to be the biggest and most ambitious yet, and she’s excited to see first-hand just how far some of it has come and meet some of the extraordinary people behind that success.” The spokesperson then recalled the couple’s previous trip to India in 2016, explaining that both have particularly fond memories of that visit. “The prince and princess are both really looking forward to what promises to be a fantastic week in India. They have such fond memories of their last visit together in 2016, and are excited to be returning a decade later.”.

Sources indicate that as mentioned, the most important diplomatic event of the tour took place on November 18 in New Delhi, where Prince William and Kate met with Prime Minister Narendra Modi. This was the only occasion during the visit when the royal couple left Mumbai, the city that hosted most of their scheduled engagements. Modi returned to the Indian capital specifically for this occasion after attending a major international summit in Manila, Philippines, to take part in the bilateral talks.

Sources indicate that A spokesperson for Kensington Palace had emphasized the strategic importance of relations between the two countries, characterized by deep and ever-growing ties in numerous sectors, which include trade, investment, defense, security, technology, education, and culture. Kate’s presence alongside William during the meeting was considered particularly significant. “This meeting reflects the importance of that relationship, as well as the role their royal highnesses can play in celebrating and strengthening the ties between our two countries.”.

Industry observers note that “For the prince, it also represents another significant engagement as he continues to take on a growing role on the international stage. We’ve seen him increasingly support the UK’s diplomatic relationships through his overseas engagements, and this meeting will provide an opportunity to build on those connections at the highest level.”.

The Prince of Wales on the Mumbai Metro.

India, after all, holds a special place in the history of relations between the British monarchy and the Commonwealth. King Charles has visited the country numerous times, on both official and private occasions, strengthening a personal and institutional relationship over the years. For William and Catherine, however, this trip represented an opportunity to build a direct relationship with a nation destined to play an increasingly key role in the international balance of power.

A close-up of the Prince and Princess of Wales.

In a recent development, with a population of over 1.4 billion people, India is now the world’s most populous country and one of the fastest-growing economies. Hosting the Earthshot Prize meant engaging a potentially massive audience on issues of environmental sustainability, resource conservation, and innovative solutions to combat climate change.

A beautiful image of the Prince and Princess of Wales.

For William and Kate, returning to India also meant revisiting a country to which they are bound by personal memories. As mentioned, their last visit was in April 2016, when the Prince and Princess of Wales—then the Duke and Duchess of Cambridge—undertook an official tour of India and Bhutan at the request of the British government. During that trip, they visited Mumbai, met with representatives from India’s cultural and sports communities, and traveled to Agra, where they admired the Taj Mahal.

It has been revealed that right in front of the famous mausoleum—a symbol of eternal love—William and Kate sat on the same white marble bench where, 24 years earlier, Lady Diana, Princess of Wales, posed during a visit to India. That photograph of Diana, portrayed alone in front of the monument, became one of the most iconic images of her public life. Taken in 1992, when her marriage to Charles was going through a deep crisis, many interpreted it as a visual representation of her loneliness. In 2016, William and Kate’s decision to recreate that shot inevitably brought Diana to mind, adding a personal and symbolic dimension to their visit.

According to recent reports, for Catherine, therefore, this trip is above all a latest step on her journey back to public life following her illness. Not a demonstration of recovery to be celebrated as a race against time, but an opportunity to resume playing an key role while moving at her own pace. And to stand once again alongside William on a mission that concerns not only the future of the monarchy, but also that of the planet.

The Prince and Princess of Wales in 2016.

Why can't you play darts in GTA 6 when you could in previous games? Because Rockstar "didn't have the resources" to do it to a standard it'd be happy with

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Nelson told VGC: "The darts one is a contentious one.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that if you've been a fan of Grand Theft Auto for a while, you might have noticed a strange absence in GTA 6. While the game is packed full of different activities, the recurring pastime of darts is missing, having been present in GTA 5, GTA Online, and GTA 4.

The reason for the lack of darts in Grand Theft Auto 6? Well, according to Rockstar North co-studio lead Rob Nelson, it's a simple case of Rockstar having too little time and resources to make it to a high standard.

Nelson told VGC: "The darts one is a contentious one. Even we... You hear they have unlimited money or unlimited time, even we do not and so sometimes you just have to admit we are not going to be able to make this to the level we feel we need to.".

Nelson elaborated that since Red Dead Redemption 2, Rockstar has taken to expanding what were small mini-games into full-on activities. He pointed to basketball in GTA 6 as an example, which you can play in a way that feels like an extension of gameplay with "fluid" movement. Even if it's a relatively small chunk of the game, a lot of time went into making it feel like "a game in its own right", Nelson remarked. And the same is true of pool.

In a recent development, "A lot of work [is needed] to get it tuned right. Darts is one we just didn't get to," Nelson stated. The studio "didn't have the resources" to include it in the game and have it up to par. "It's better not to do it than to do it and have it not be good enough," he said.

According to recent reports, even without darts, there are plenty of side activities in Grand Theft Auto 6 that help expand Vice City. This includes diving and treasure hunting and fishing, both of which you unlock near the start of the game. If you're looking for a guide of all there is to do in the game, Eurogamer's GTA 6 walkthrough is a good place to start. We've also got a breakdown of all the GTA 6 cheats if you needed an extra hand getting through the game.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, avengers: Doomsday is packed with heroes and villains from the past quarter-century of Marvel movies. But there's one all-powerful figure who is quite clearly being held back – and it's got fans wondering what (if anything) he will have to do in the upcoming battle against Doctor Doom.

Sources indicate that so, how do you solve a problem like Bob? The character, first introduced in Thunderbolts, is currently lying dormant and chilling at New Avengerz HQ after being twisted into Sentry, a Superman-like figure who can send people to The Void with but a mere thought. Can you really leave that on the table if you're going up against Doom?

Well, it's a discussion that has spilled over to Reddit, with audiences debating the ramifications of unleashing Bob onto the world.

"Sentry is obviously gonna be there as an absolute last resort since the Avengers probably don’t wanna risk the Void coming back until they have no other choice," one said.

It has been revealed that another added, "Doom is a master manipulator. Giving him access to the Sentry/Void is like a death invitation.".

Sources indicate that others joke that Bob will simply be Bob for the entirety of Avengers: Doomsday, kicking his feet and doing the dishes while the rest of the team brings the fight to Doom. There's a suggestion, though, that any major deaths – including to Florence Pugh's Yelena – would turn Bob into the unstoppable Sentry once more, with no allies to help calm him down this time.

Personally, I think Bob is being held back just to continue the age-old question of 'Who would win in a fight?' Pitting Sentry against Doom too soon not only risks answering it, but risks making Bob's power level seem diminished when he could be saved instead of Avengers: Secret Wars.

Discover what happens next – and if Bob puts on the Sentry suit once more – in Avengers: Doomsday, out in the UK on December 16 and in the US on December 18.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In the wake of Grand Theft Auto 6's release and the wave of glowing reviews it received, a war is raging in Metacritic's user reviews, with some of the medium's best games of all time caught in the crossfire.

If you take a look at Metacritics' best games of all time list, you'll see Grand Theft Auto 6 sitting pretty at the top spot. Yet, if you take a gander at some of the others following close behind it, you may notice a sudden increase in very negative reviews from those riding hard for Rockstar's latest release.

According to recent reports, take the user reviews for The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, which held the top spot for years prior to GTA 6's launch. You can see such pearls of wisdom as: "L Japanese Propaganda. GTA 6 better grafics **** it loser Japanese people," from a user called. Mimm1. Or this gem from danzerthethird: "ass nhbgvfyghjgvfghbjnbhgfycvgjbhguytguyhuytyfgutfgyrc7fytghugytfughtvfygbhjgfycurtyvghbgvfycutryvgcfrgv.".

Sources indicate that the same is true for the original Soul Calibur. Its user reviews includes newly delivered pieces of critique like this from user GTABEST2456: "Slop game dethroned by GTA 6, 99 on metacritic N1, now this is third LOOOOOOL, get rekt. I played through and I wish there was less zelda references more niko bellic.".

Sources indicate that even Super Mario Galaxy 2 wasn't safe. Consumers have taken to review- bombing this game too, an example being BoroqueTsunami who wrote: "Peak Nintendoslop ️ Jump man gimmick. Y'all thought it was sweet until Rockstar pulled up." All of these reviews, across all these non-GTA 6 games, were written following the release of Grand Theft Auto 6.

While it is unclear whether GTA 6 fans shot the first bullet here, or whether anti-GTA 6 Metacritic brigaders are to blame, what is apparent is GTA 6 is itself being hit with a counter-offensive of sorts. "Retaliation for Zelda review bombing," wrote user Lucius26. "I didn't choose this war, but I'll fight it all the same. GTA fans, we were not your enemy. GTA6 just made people mad. You like a bad game, accept that.".

This is all obviously silly and only helps to make the user review section of Metacritic less helpful for people actually trying to get a gist of what these games are like from members of the public. This also stems from a lack of verification on whether people have actually played these games before writing their takes.

Sources indicate that whether events like this will prompt Metacritic to implement some additional quality control remains to be seen, though it has been a continuous problem for a while now and this is hardly the first time review-bombing has been used by some of the more bizarre fans of substantial-budget releases. In fairness, Metacritic is not the only platform to have suffered from this. Steam, too, has had a history of user review-bombing, with Valve adding features to help curb this over the years.

According to recent reports, 9-1-1 has officially wrapped up the first half of its 10th season on the 2026 TV schedule, and it was anything but calm. Thursday’s fall finale included some intense calls, and even more intense scenes between Buck and Eddie as their latest fallout continues. The best friends have not really been on the same page for a while now, and I’ve been worried about them. Luckily, the executive producer is explaining where things stand with them following the midseason finale.

Buck’s big decision in the Season 9 finale to foster his biological son following the death of his parents has led to some difficulties at the start of Season 10. It doesn’t help that after Buck decided to give Theo up, Eddie became his foster dad through emergency placement. This has put even more pressure on them, and EP and showrunner Tim Minear told TV Insider why they went in this direction:.

I think conflict is drama, obviously, but it felt… To me, it was sort of an interesting way to have Eddie come in and take Buck’s story away from him in a sense. They both have stories, right? Obviously, Theo is Buck’s biological kid. Buck had every good intention of fostering and growing into that role, which he still has an opportunity to do. But also, I just believe that Eddie would not let that kid go into a group home. And I think there was some truth in what Buck remarked about Eddie’s guilt about being ambivalent about his own son in the first five years of his life.

In a recent development, buck had donated sperm to his friend and his wife, who were having trouble conceiving a few seasons ago, and after helping her deliver, it didn’t really come up again...until last season. Then, after the couple died in a car crash, Buck felt responsible for the kid and took him in. There was some concern for Buck going into Season 10, and it was obvious this wasn’t going to be easy, especially after seeing Theo’s chaotic energy. So he ultimately believed that Theo would be better with someone else.

However, Minear is right in believing that Eddie, who was the only one who knew what Buck was doing, wouldn’t let Theo go to a group home. Unfortunately, this creates more conflict between them, but it’s what makes the situation more realistic:.

So again, a lot of the stories here this season — look, we’re in Season 10, and a lot of the stories this season are an accumulation of canon that we’ve built up over the past decade with these characters. And that always makes for a richer story, it seems to me. But I actually think Buck and Eddie, conflict is natural, particularly between people who are really close. Nobody can piss you off as much as someone who you’re really close to, and I just think that’s real.

Despite the growing tension in the midseason finale, Buck and Eddie had somewhat made up towards the end of the episode. While Buck wasn’t quite ready to see Theo, he understood why Eddie did what he did. It’s hard to tell where things will go for them in the newly introduced year, but with Theo staying with Eddie and Buck coming to terms with everything, it should be interesting. On that note, Minear shares that both of them will have some growing to do for multiple reasons:.

Sources indicate that yeah, I think they’re at an interstitial stage where Buck sees that it is really best for Theo right now to be with Eddie. Maybe neither one of them handled it perfectly, but if they handled it perfectly, then you’d have a five-episode season as opposed to 18. But I think they’re in a good place in their friendship. I think that Theo becomes a spoiler a little bit, and until Buck feels like he can walk into that house and face that kid, there’s kind of a natural barrier there between whatever kind of closeness that he can enjoy with Eddie off the job.

Sources indicate that I have been worried about Buck and Eddie’s relationship since the beginning of the season, when it was clear that Buck fostering Theo would bring some problems. And it didn’t get any easier when Eddie became the foster parent. I’m definitely glad that they’ve crossed a barrier, and they both realize how they acted in this situation might not have been the best. However, I am looking forward to seeing what happens now that they have an understanding with each other and Theo.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

9-1-1 is now on its winter hiatus, but the series will return on Thursday, January 7 at 8 p.m. ET on ABC, streaming the next day on Hulu.

Passionate writer. Obsessed with anything and everything entertainment, specifically movies and television. Can get easily attached to fictional characters.

Breaking: GTA 6 can run at 60fps on Xbox Series X if you use a glitch, but there's a catch

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (393 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that grand Theft Auto 6 runs at 30 frames-per-second across all the consoles it's currently available on, including the more powerful PlayStation 5 Pro.
  • In a recent development, reddit user Meowwie64 devised a way to essentially unlock GTA 6's frame-rate on Series X.
  • According to recent reports, in a detailed post, Meowwie64 shared the steps they used to trigger their glitch.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that grand Theft Auto 6 runs at 30 frames-per-second across all the consoles it's currently available on, including the more powerful PlayStation 5 Pro. The game doesn't offer a 60fps performance mode or an option to unlock the frame-rate, but one industrious player has managed to do it anyway on Xbox.

In a recent development, reddit user Meowwie64 devised a way to essentially unlock GTA 6's frame-rate on Series X. Their hack relied on the Xbox's rarely-discussed Quick Resume feature, which lets you park multiple games in memory and switch between them without having to re-load each game.

According to recent reports, in a detailed post, Meowwie64 shared the steps they used to trigger their glitch. For starters, you're going to need a 120Hz monitor display or TV, as the glitch requires adjusting refresh rates.

First, you need to limit Xbox to display at 60Hz under the console Settings menu. Then, you start GTA 6 (version 01.002.001), wait until the six-star logo appears and then go back to Xbox Settings to change the refresh rate to 120Hz.

Before you return to GTA 6, the final step requires launching another game on your console. This has to be a cold boot, meaning the game shouldn't already be running parked in Quick Resume.

According to recent reports, after the second game rolls out, you now need to use Quick Resume to resume playing GTA 6, which is when you're going to notice the higher frame-rate. The Reddit user said the game could reach 90-plus FPS at certain moments.

Unfortunately, the user also discovered that game-speed appears to be tied to frame-rate in GTA 6, at least when it comes to certain gameplay animations and when performing certain actions. "I have a stable 90fps and everything works fine but Jason's animations run at 2x speed or more," Meowwie64 wrote. Incidentally, cutscenes do not appear to be affected by this problem, so they run at their normal speed.

In a recent development, as much as a 30fps frame-rate makes GTA 6 feel less smooth and potentially less enjoyable to play compared to 60fps or higher, none of the current-generation consoles are capable of delivering frame-rates beyond that. Tech experts Digital Foundry recently explained why even the PS5 Pro isn't powerful enough to run the game at 60fps or even 40fps.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The world wants me to write more about Grand Theft Auto 6 and I bravely answer "No". Last week, I obtained 50% of the endings available in Queen's Domain, the best videogame to release in the year 2026. The next 50% require, well, a lot of nook-scouring and cranny-uncovering—many more hours of gameplay which I am preserving for myself as a Christmas holiday treat.

Recent findings suggest that and when I do, I suspect I might make a little (just a little) use of this rad Queen's Domain map by a creator called Leny15. Barely a week ago I wrote that "I suspect a cross-section of [Queen's Domain's] goliath, entwined map would make for a killer bit of wall art". Well, I was right. Here it is and it looks rad as hell.

Industry observers note that no, really. Even if you're not a Queen's Domain player—or maybe especially if you're not—take a look at this thing. It's one thing to wander these maps as a player, it's another to get a totally flexible birdseye view of how dense, twisty and interconnected they are. I will never stop being blown away by how knotty and elaborate this game is; I love it.

I will also never believe I have actually explored all of it. I'll be honest, gang, I really feel like I've plumbed the depths of this game, but this map has entries for areas I ain't even heard of, and even those areas that I have heard of seem to contain secret sub-areas I've barely touched.

My favourite feature of this thing has got to be the ability to upload your save to it, at which point it will give you a completion percentage and tick off the collectibles and secrets you've already attained (reminder that you can download your Steam cloud saves right in your browser). I was heartened to read that I have, it seems, done in about 70% of this game already. I was even more heartened to learn that the remaining 30% seems even stranger, more complicated, and more baffling than all the rest. I can't wait to check it out.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Gaming tech giant Nvidia has decided to reinstate Jensen Huang as its president and CEO, despite allegedly saying it wouldn't, and despite a string of extramarital affairs and investigations into alleged bullying, workplace harassment, and humiliation.

"The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," Nvidia's Chair Harvey C. Jones revealed on behalf of the Nvidia's board today - the same person reported as saying the board "does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO".

Sources indicate that "We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Company. We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as Nvidia's chief financial officer.".

In the same press release, Huang stated he was "honoured" to return to the organization "at the beginning of a fresh industrial revolution". "I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment," Huang said.

However, the investigation into one of Huang's extramarital affairs - the one with the person US intelligence believes to be a Chinese spy - will "proceed to conclusion". The organization also stated it formed a "National Security and Export Control Committee", with independent directors, in relation to this.

Sources indicate that huang resigned on 12th November a few days after his affair with the alleged Chinese spy came to light. Two subsequent affairs - both stated to be with Nvidia employees and therefore his subordinates - were unearthed not long after, putting increased pressure on Huang and Nvidia.

Since his departure, Nvidia stock has tanked, and as news of his reinstatement spreads around the world, it has sharply recovered again.

Grand Theft Auto 6 leaker Cyberleek appears to have followed through on their threat to release the executable of the Xbox build of GTA 6 they put into the wild last week, calling it "an early Christmas gift" for followers and explicitly linking the leak to efforts to recreate the game on PC: "The torch passes to the open source recomp and emulation projects.".

Industry observers note that cyberleek released a near-complete build of GTA 6 late last week, holding back only the main exe—the part that makes everything else run, basically—until either their crypto coin achieved a $15 million market cap, or November 23, whichever came first. The crypto missed badly, but time marches on, and so here we are.

It has been revealed that the release of the exe, naturally, includes a call for more "donations" in its readme file (via Reddit) which Cyberleek remarked will go toward a secretive project "for the gamers." They also taunted Take-Two Interactive's efforts to track them down: "Months of takedowns, subpoenas and wallet tracing later, the hunt is still on and the uploads keep arriving. No budget makes a lock unbreakable, and no court order deletes what the internet already has.".

It has been revealed that leaks in the game industry aren't anything new, but this case is unique: GTA 6, effectively the biggest videogame of all time, still hasn't been announced for PC, as is Take-Two's way. But the advent of AI means the game could be emulated on our platform far more quickly than was possible in the past—some modders estimated it could happen within a week.

One of the leads on the Leonida recomp project predicted that things will start to move promptly from here:.

At the same time, Shayder tempered expectations in a message on the Leonida Discord, saying "it will take at least a week" for the project to reach the point where GTA will be playable on PC.

How that unofficial emulated made-with-AI build would compare to the real deal is an open question, and I strongly suspect the answer will be "not well," but even just having something GTA 6-ish playable on PC is a headache that I'm pretty sure Take-Two would rather not have to deal with. I also wonder whether it will prompt Take-Two to release GTA 6 on PC more promptly than it has with previous releases. A rumor to that effect surfaced in October and I had serious doubts, but it's possible that ongoing emulation efforts will expedite its arrival..

  • Industry observers note that if the holiday season has wrapped by February 14, the weeks following are the shoulder season.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that why do we let something like the calendar dictate our holidays? The fact that Thanksgiving and Christmas are just four weeks apart means by the time you’ve returned from November family visits, unpacked, shopped, decorated, done the party circuit, bought gifts, and maybe—maybe—worked for a few days, you have to turn around and celebrate again. It’s exhausting and expensive and too warp-speed to feel like that much of a good time. I’m not arguing to ban Christmas—which I am using as a catchall for nondenominational winter holidays, however that looks to you—what I am proposing is, in fact, much more exciting. I think we should switch the dates of Christmas and Valentine’s Day.

Sources indicate that consider it! Instead of condensing so much effort and so much merriment into such a ludicrously small window at the very end of the year with nothing but the bland hell of winter ahead of us, let’s maximize our time by stretching it out. Valentine’s Day is for romance, whether that means watching Bridget Jones’s Diary with friends, eating overpriced meals at candlelit restaurants, making cards, or mainlining chocolates. So on December 24, celebrate platonic love with friends—à la Galentine’s Day, except we should think of a better name—and maybe go on a date on the 25th. If that date goes well: bam! You now have a plus-one to a Upcoming Year’s Eve party and a midnight make out partner.

Industry observers note that if the holiday season has wrapped by February 14, the weeks following are the shoulder season. Life is slow. But by the time everyone trickles back home from watching Die Hard in their pajamas or shopping post-Christmas sales or going to the gym, you only have to survive one month until the sweet relief of spring in late March. Nothing makes more sense for how to survive the long nights and cold of winter.

It has been revealed that so we go all-in on spring. Mid-April is when it likely won’t snow again; around then you no longer need heat—at least in Newly introduced York City—so let’s make that a national holiday celebrating warm weather with seasonal bouquets (tulips, lilacs, peonies), foraged ramps, and maybe specials on dry-cleaning winter coats or sales on shearling boots.

But why stop there? We in America could take a page from France, where May can have four(!) public holidays as a kind of summer practice run. I’d be more than happy to celebrate VE Day in solidarity: Liberté, égalité, holiday! In our version, maybe botanical gardens will be free to the public for picnics. Maybe amusement parks will be gratis? Maybe lobster rolls and strawberry shortcake will be handed out on the street? Can the first summer blockbuster of May be an annual event with free popcorn? This month of long weekends will culminate in Memorial Day barbecues, which is a perfect bookend to summer with Labor Day—no notes.

Let’s keep summer luxurious, so summer Fridays will not be at the discretion of employers but mandated by the government for those three months. The Fourth of July can stay where it is with the caveat that if it rains, we get to observe it on the next day forecast for hot dog weather. Nothing important happens in August—phone it in, federal holiday or not. Labor Day stays, of course. The week following it in Upcoming York is Fashion Week, which runs concurrently with the US Open for tennis—very busy but very social. We’re going to adopt that nationwide as a festive season soft launching the country into fall.

And finally, let’s turn our attention to that somber stretch of time between early September and Thanksgiving. We don’t get enough time off, so we will move Presidents’ Day from February to mid-October for another much-needed holiday. Then cook a massive turkey dinner on Thanksgiving, see your extended family, watch football, whatever, and delight in the fact that you don’t have to do it again until February. But start figuring out your Valentine’s Day dates now—those prix fixe dinners with chocolate lava cakes really book up fast these days.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rockstar just issued a fresh patch for GTA 6 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S, targeting a few issues players have been reporting since the game debuted last Thursday (19th November).

The 23rd November patch for the game deploys seven major fixes for the game, including a pretty significant bug that prevented phone calls not triggering at certain points, resulting in a scenario where you could be locked out of progressing the game. The official update is titled 'version 01.002.002', and its weighs in at different sizes on different consoles: it's 603.8 MB on PS5, and 1.6 GB on Xbox Series X/S.

Thanks to an update on the Rockstar website, you can read all of the updates that arrive with the latest pathc below.

Recent findings suggest that there have been a few fairly high-profile cases of the autosave not working as the developer intended, leading to a few cases of streamers losing plenty of real-world time thanks to unpredictable auto-save behaviour. JasonTheWeen lost 12 hours of progress on the PS5, for example.

It has been revealed that but there's one matter here the developer hasn't addressed: vignetting. Plenty of players have taken to online communities to complain about the vignette effect that pops into the game - theoretically to help with motion smoothing and various grapihcal elements as the game runs in 30FPS. THe effect is worsened when you're fatigued, hungry, or have some other status effect, but it is present quite a lot of the time, too. Most of the responses to a tweet about the patch posted by the Rockstar Support account reference the vignetting in GTA 6, and the developer has issued no response at the time of writing.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As Dawn of War 4's December release date inches ever closer, a fresh trailer appears to have teased a fan-favourite character's inclusion in the RTS's first post-launch DLC.

The trailer, which covers the Commander Edition of Dawn of War 4, includes a breakdown of all the extra stuff packed in alongside this version of the game. This includes the digital soundtrack, three-days of early-access to the game, and the story prologue. It'll also include the Aftermath post-launch DLC too, with its dedicated campaign and upcoming playable faction.

Now, ever since the Aftermath DLC was declared, people have speculated it would be chaos-focused. The design of the DLC logo is black with a gold trim, an often-used colour scheme for the faction. However, which sort of Chaos was left up to debate. That is, until this trailer, where the answer is seemingly given away with a cheeky tease.

It has been revealed that in its final few seconds, the trailer shows a pair of glowing yellow mechanical eyes peering out from a gloomy background. This was rapidly identified as almost-certainly Vashtorr the Arkifane, a relatively upcoming addition to Warhammer 40,000 and a fan-favourite baddie all around.

Vashtorr as a character has been getting a lot of love ever since his introduction in 2023. It was then, during the Arks of Omen campaign for the tabletop game, that he played a central part in the narrative event bridging the game's 10th and 11th edition. Since then he was the main antagonist of Boltgun 2, and was central in the 2025 novel Achmagos.

What this means for Dawn of War 4 is that, if he is a commander of Chaos forces, expect a lot of machinery and demon engines on his side. That's kind of his whole deal. Whether that means he's paired with tech-focused Dark Mechanicum as a sort of mirror to the Adeptus Mechanicus faction already in the game, or if he'll come alongside Chaos Space Marines to better reflect the Dark Angels / Blood Ravens remains to be seen. It could also be a mix of both! We'll have to wait and see.
