📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that nvidia has announced that Jensen Huang has been reinstated as president and CEO of Nvidia, while he'll also return to the Board of Directors. This is happening just hours after US President Donald Trump said Huang should come back. "The Board of Directors voted unanimously to reinstate Mr. Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with Mr. Huang, after which the Board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead Nvidia," the technology giant said. "In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang's reinstatement poses no national security risk." Nvidia chair of the Board Harvey C. Jones said the Board believes "Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners, and customers." "We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Firm. We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as Nvidia's Chief Financial Officer," he added. Trump said in a social media post that Nvidia's Board made "the correct and proper decision" to bring Huang back. Trump went on to say that the US government has no real to believe that Huang's return "poses any risk to national security." https://twitter.com/TheStalwart/status/2124868325524054057 For his part, Huang said he is honored to return to Nvidia to lead what he called "one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a latest industrial revolution." "I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support. Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can’t wait to get back to work.” Huang was ousted from Nvidia earlier this month after it came to light that he had a romantic relationship with a person that sources said was possibly a spy for China, though no hard evidence was ever provided to back this up. It was later reported that Huang had multiple other affairs with people he worked with. In response to the reports, Nvidia formed a committee made up of independent directors who had the job of investigating the "foreign intelligence" claims. Additionally, the committee hired an independent attorney to assist, and that investigation remains ongoing, with Huang's support. In addition to the internal investigation, there are multiple other open cases against Nvidia, including a probe by the SEC over financial accounting claims. In response to the entire situation, Nvidia has also created a new National Security and Export Control Committee to "oversee trade complicance and national security risks." Prior to today, Nvidia's board said it had no intention of bringing Huang back, but things can change fast. For his part, Huang said he would be "honored" to return as Nvidia's CEO. The Nvidia controversies led to turmoil in the stock market, in part because Nvidia is one of the “Mag 7” companies that are driving growth in the US. Some of the information coming to light suggests that Nvidia’s accounting and export control compliance are not buttoned up, and this has fueled further concerns about the growth potential and returns on investment for the AI trade. Numerous other technology and AI stocks have dropped in value significantly since the Nvidia news broke. Now that Huang is back as CEO, though, not only is Nvidia's stock price ripping, but the market overall--not just AI and tech stocks--is seeing positive upwards trends.

Every Version of 'A Christmas Carol,' Ranked (and Where to Stream Them)

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that charles Dickens’ A Christmas Carol is the greatest story about Christmas ever written—even better than the one with Mary and Joseph and the manger.
  • I've carefully considered every major theatrical and TV adaptation of A Christmas Carol and rated each in terms of holiday spirit, Dickensian whimsy, and Scrooge-osity to arrive at the definite, no-argument-possible best-to-worst list of Christmas Carols.
  • To rank Christmas Carols, you have to decide what A Christmas Carol is to you.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that charles Dickens’ A Christmas Carol is the greatest story about Christmas ever written—even better than the one with Mary and Joseph and the manger. The 1843 tale of a miser browbeaten by self-righteous ghosts is (probably) the most filmed story of all time. Dozens of cinematic adaptations of A Christmas Carol have been released in theaters and on TV since Scrooge; or Marley's Ghost came out in 1901. Hundreds or thousands if you count re-imaginings and very special episodes of sitcoms. But which version is the very best?

I've carefully considered every major theatrical and TV adaptation of A Christmas Carol and rated each in terms of holiday spirit, Dickensian whimsy, and Scrooge-osity to arrive at the definite, no-argument-possible best-to-worst list of Christmas Carols.

To rank Christmas Carols, you have to decide what A Christmas Carol is to you. My criteria for inclusion: It has to be full-length (at least around an hour long); it has to have been released widely, either in theaters, on network television, or through a larger streaming service, and it has to be fairly close to a direct adaptation—modernizations, re-imaginings, sequels, and that episode of The Six Million Dollar Man don’t count (sorry, Scrooged fans). Using those criteria, I’ve winnowed the Carols down to the 17 you see below, ranked from best to worst, along with where you can stream each one.

Industry observers note that it's tough to pick a single adaptation of A Christmas Carol as the absolute best of all time, but the 1984 TV movie version starring George C. Scott is unassailable. Other versions do some things better, but this one does everything right—no mistakes. It stays close to the original text; it's perfectly produced; and it has a consistency of tone and vision that makes it the most balanced of all versions of the story. A Christmas Carol might not have the best Scrooge of all time, but George C. Scott's performance is a solid nine out of ten, and this version features the most adorable and pitiable Tiny Tim of all and the best Ghost of Christmas Present, played by Edward Woodward, who played the policeman in The Wicker Man.

Where to stream it: Roku, Tubi, Pluto TV.

Shot in the midst of the Great Depression, the first sound version of A Christmas Carol digs deeper into the despair and horror of the story than any other adaptation. It’s a bleak, German expressionist Christmas flick, and Seymour Hicks’ sickly, haunted portrayal of Ebenezer Scrooge fits the tone perfectly. Instead of delighting in his own crapulence, Hicks plays Scrooge like Satan in The Divine Comedy—he's not the ruler of Hell; he's its most tormented prisoner. Scrooge's miserliness is played as pathology. He wears dirty, torn clothing and shivers miserably while eating gruel because he can’t bring himself to burn a single scrap of coal. Even when he converts, it seems like a manic episode instead of Christmas spirit, suggesting this could be a story about an old man going mad.

Where to stream: Sadly, the version on free streaming services like Tubi and Plex is colorized, but you can watch it on YouTube in glorious black and white.

Industry observers note that this major-budget musical take on the Yuletide classic turns Dickens up to 11. Scrooge is huge, a raucous, crowd-pleasing musical with hundreds of extras, elaborate sets, and a scenery-chewing central performance from Albert Finney to hold it all together. But Finney and company also manage to keep the emotional core of the story intact. The music is great, with memorable tunes like “I Hate People,” a song that Finney snarls instead of sings. Scrooge has the best ghosts of any version of A Christmas Carol, too—you can't beat the cheesy awesomeness of big-money 1970s special effects.

Where to stream it: Tubi, Pluto TV, Plex.

According to recent reports, before Hallmark devoted its corporate life to forgettable holiday-themed romantic comedies, it co-produced one of the best versions of A Christmas Carol ever made. This entire movie belongs to Patrick Stewart, whose nuanced, layered portrayal of Scrooge is the best that has ever been done. His "conversion" scene is so visceral and honest, it brought a tear to my eyes, even though I've seen the exact scene performed in at least 40 other movies, stage plays, and episodes of 1980s sitcoms. Sadly, the paucity of basic cable budgets in the 1990s results in some chintzy-looking sets and laughable special effects that mar an otherwise top-notch production.

Where to stream it: Digital rental only.

Horror director Ti West's Carol adaptation muddies the moral clarity of Dickens' tale and suggests there's something deeply troubling beneath all the Victorian holiday catharsis. With a few exceptions, Ebenezer hits the familiar beats of A Christmas Carol: It delivers the crowd-pleasing rich-jerk-turns-good story moviegoers expect, but West layers in subtle hints along the way that suggest the floorboards are rotten, and if you dance with Christmas joy too hard, you'll fall into the dark basement below. Ebenezer seems to whisper to audiences, "How much does the conversion of one miserly wretch matter in the face of systemic injustice? And isn't he going to snap out of it when the fright wears off anyway?" Bonus: As you'd probably expect from a Ti West movie, the ghosts are genuinely scary.

Where to watch it: In theaters now.

I'm sticking A Muppet Christmas Carol randomly here on the list because you can't reasonably compare it to other versions of the story. The Muppet version is a thing unto itself. Like the Ol' Dirty Bastard, its style has no father. A Muppet Christmas Carol is absolutely delightful from start to finish, for children, grown-ups, cats, dogs, space aliens, and anything else you got. It shouldn't even work to set Michael Caine's serious portrayal of Ebenezer Scrooge against a supporting cast of puppets, but somehow it all seems natural.

It has been revealed that alastair Sim takes Ebenezer Scrooge on a real journey in this movie. In the first act, he plays Scrooge like Capitalism personified, an uncaring, amoral monument to pure acquisition. He seems like a Scrooge who'd scare away ghosts, but when Marley reveals up dragging his trademark chains, Sim is instantly reduced to pop-eyed fear, like the single chink in his armor is the supernatural. Scrooge then regresses to a childlike, bashful figure as ghosts lead him to different visions, finally emerging from his symbolic death to his rebirth as a Christmas-obsessed guy who lives to serve others. This movie might be among the best of the genre, but an unnecessary subplot about Scrooge's business sandbags the movie through part of the second act.

Mr. Magoo's Christmas Carol was the first animated version of A Christmas Carol and the first animated holiday special ever shown on American TV. The main character, Mr. Magoo, was the star of a one-joke, limited-animation cartoon popular in the early 1960s about an old man who couldn’t see very well, so it’s surprising how carefully crafted and effective this version of A Christmas Carol is. It's weirdly meta too: Jim Backus voices Mr. Magoo, who is a (blind) actor performing as Scrooge in A Christmas Carol on Broadway, so the play is bookended with "this guy can't see!" bits. The songs are strange, memorable and funny (listen to "Razzleberry Dressing" above once and you'll never forget it), but the emotional core of the story remains surprisingly powerful. Jim Backus is amazing.

Where to stream it: Peacock, Roku, Tubi.

I'm breaking my own rule about not including shortened versions of the story because this animated Carol is that great. Its evocative, graceful, hand-drawn look belongs to animation legend Richard Williams and was inspired by the illustrations from the original version of A Christmas Carol. It's a cartoon, but it's not a kiddie cartoon, so the darkness of the ghosts isn't glossed over. Plus, Scrooge is voiced by Alastair Sim, reprising his role from 1951's Scrooge.

Industry observers note that there's nothing wrong with this brightly lit, by-the-numbers take on A Christmas Carol, but it seems designed to appeal to as broad an audience as possible, so the rough edges of the story have been sanded off. The ghosts aren’t that scary. Scrooge isn’t that miserly, etc. It’s fine for a Christmas movie to be lighthearted fun, but the lowered stakes ultimately blunt the emotional resonance of the climax, leading to a mediocre Christmas Carol.

Recent findings suggest that I'm including this version of A Christmas Carol because it's Lifehacker editor Meghan Walbert's favorite. Sorry, Meghan, but this flimsy 1970s TV movie adaptation hasn't aged well. Henry Winkler does a good job as Scrooge, and it's cool to see Burgess Meredith and other old-timey stars, but overall, this is a schmaltzy, plodding film that unwisely replaces a lot of Dickens' best writing with the work of 1970s TV hacks.

Where to stream it: Pluto, Tubi, Amazon Prime.

According to recent reports, I really wanted to like Disney’s A Christmas Carol. Robert Zemeckis is a great director and Jim Carrey is a force of nature, but I couldn't get through it. There might be a lot to recommend this version of the story, but using 2009’s technology to create realistic-looking characters was such a puzzling choice. The whole movie looks like a video game cutscene from a PS3 game, and I kept wanting to hit “A” to skip ahead to the gameplay.

Recent findings suggest that it doesn't seem like the producers of this obscure 2012 straight-to-streaming feature had much money to work with, which is too bad. If they had, they might have been able to better realize some of the intriguing ideas behind this movie. It's a straight-up horror take on the tale, but it just isn't scary. Sadly, you can't carry a feature film on good intentions. Overall, a swing and a miss.

Where to stream it: Tubi, Amazon Prime.

Recent findings suggest that the animation in this 1997 musical cartoon version of A Christmas Carol is dated, pedestrian, and ugly. The songs are forgettable, and Scrooge has a pet bulldog for some reason. (The one good joke is that he named his dog "Debit.") It’s just not good, which is a shame, because the cast is overflowing with talent, including Tim Curry as Scrooge, Ed Asner, and Whoopi Goldberg.

Where to stream it: Roku, Pluto TV, Xumo.

This BBC drama goes for a philosophical, moody version of Scrooge, but it doesn’t come together. It’s dark, grim, and so ponderously self-serious that it collapses under its own weight. In an effort to present aspects of A Christmas Carol that haven't been seen before (like "How Marley got his chains"), A Christmas Carol rewrites the original text from the ground up, but it comes across like Dickens' first draft with a bad case of Surf Dracula.

Where to stream it: Hulu, Disney+.

Sources indicate that the current state of Dickens adaptation is not good. Netflix's uninspired, sappy, CGI version of A Christmas Carol tries to tart the story up with slapstick, songs, and jokes, but it’s all cynical, lowest-common-denominator horseshit. The dialogue has been dumbed down and joked up. Scrooge has a silly dog for comic relief. They added scatological humor. Think about this: The minds behind Scrooge: A Christmas Carol read Dickens and concluded, “This story would be better with a wacky dog and fart jokes.”.

It has been revealed that A Christmas Carol is such a solid story, even a grade-school production of it can be fun to watch. But a cynical production of it is extra terrible, given the message of the story. This terrible ego project is a bottom-of-the-barrel Christmas Carol because it feels like a money grab. Kelsey Grammer sucks as Scrooge, mugging his way through a lightweight performance. Jason Alexander sucks as Marley. Jennifer Love Hewitt is, well, actually pretty good as Scrooge’s Christmas-past romantic interest. She is a rare bright spot in this dreary movie, however. Everything else is mid to terrible. It’s shot and lit like a TV show; the sets are bland and the songs forgettable. Overall, it has the cynical feeling of assembly-line, “let’s get this shit over with” TV production.

Where to stream it: Tubi, Pluto TV, Plex.

It has been revealed that “What, is this a book that I wrote? With my own brain?” Knight teased as she pulled out a copy of her new book, The F*ck Them Theory: Self-Help for People Who Are Done Being the Bigger Person, on sale Tuesday, November 24.

Industry observers note that when asked what when was the “last time” that she was unable to apply her “f*** them theory” for professional purposes, Knight told Us, she sent a “really mean” email at 3 a.m. the night before.

Grand Theft Auto 6 has raised the bar for open-world games, and Cyberpunk 2 creative director Igor Sarzyński is feeling it. Online, the developer jokingly commented about GTA 6 setting a latest gold standard for the genre, a level of quality that makes him want to pack up his Cyberpunk 2 development bags and call it a day. "GTA 6-induced-open-world-game-dev-depression is real," Sarzyński wrote online. Probably the single greatest artistic achievement in history, I mean it. Scale, density, coherence, thoughtfulness of it all, just a technological and creative miracle. Cyberpunk 2 is canceled, Imma go sweep autumn leaves in my backyard now." https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OAN_BXmVR0g Don't worry, Cyberpunk fans, because Sarzyński believes the game will offer a unique "flavor" compared to GTA 6. "Seriously though, I think we're doing something of our own, with a different, unique flavor," he wrote in a follow-up post. "GTA is impressive in a way all great art is; it expands what is possible, a captivating vision flawlessly executed." Meanwhile, Cyberpunk 2077 has had a great 2026, as the release of the new Cyberpunk Edgerunners anime series once again drove the game's numbers up. Other developers across the industry have also commented on GTA 6, and Naughty Dog world design director Michael Barclay also believes that it is a technological achievement. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that thanksgiving is nearly upon us and, with that, avid TV viewers can look forward to plenty of programming specifically geared towards the holiday. As all of those special offerings roll in on network TV, some may be wondering what’s going on with the late-night reveals. There are now details regarding what hosts Jimmy Fallon, Jimmy Kimmel and Seth Meyers have planned for this coming week. And, from the looks of it, Fallon is differentiating himself from Kimmel over the holidays in a very keen way.

NBC – which houses both The Tonight Show and Late Night with Seth Meyers – has long capitalized on Turkey Day. After all, the storied network remains the home of the beloved Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade (which Fallon has participated in). Historically, Fallon and Meyers’ demonstrates have sought to draw in viewers even on the night of the holiday, and that’ll continue this year. Both shows will be on for T-giving amid the 2026 TV schedule, and they have some special developments planned.

Recent findings suggest that per NBC’s press site, Fallon’s Tonight Show will kick off the week of November 23 with a repeat on Monday and then run latest episodes from Tuesday to Thursday. When it comes to the Thanksgiving broadcast, Fallon is set to welcome back his old pal, Justin Timberlake, to the show for the first time in two years. Mentioned episode could lead to some memorable moments as has been the case with past T-giving broadcasts. I’m sure some devoted viewers remember Fallon and Kevin James’ messy food sketch from 2016.

Meanwhile, Seth Meyers’ Late Night will drop fresh episodes from Monday, November 23 through Thursday November 26. And, for the holiday, Meyers is continuing his tradition of having his family members on the show for Thanksgiving. Amy Poehler and Tina Fey – Meyers’ longtime friends from his SNL days – will also appear during that holiday show.

Industry observers note that it definitely tracks that NBC would want to keep these late-night offerings on the air during Thanksgiving. Not only networks are alike, though, as it seems that Jimmy Kimmel and co. at ABC are going a different route.

It has been revealed that the ABC press site confirms that Jimmy Kimmel Live! will only air fresh episodes on Monday, November 23 and Tuesday, November 24. For the remainder of the week, the show will go on a break and reruns will air in its place. So, in other words, this marks a brief hiatus for the team over at Live! Of course, such a break isn’t unheard of for this show or any other like it. What’s also worth noting is that this break comes months after Kimmel’s latest time away from the desk.

In a recent development, over the summer, Kimmel took some time off, and that’s something he’s done over the past several years. During that time, his show remains on the air, though, and a cavalcade of guest hosts are brought in each week until Kimmel returns. Those guest host stints can be quite eventful (as viewers learned when Tiffany Haddish hosted back in July).

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

Recent findings suggest that when it comes to these Thanksgiving strategies, though, there definitely doesn’t seem to be anything too out of the ordinary. Jimmy Kimmel’s show can also seemingly afford to take a little time off, given the show has been crushing in the ratings, especially in the aftermath of The Late Show’s cancellation. (We’ll tear off a drumstick in your honor, Stephen Colbert.) All in all, though, I’m interested in seeing what Jimmy Fallon’s The Tonight Show and Seth Meyers’ Late Night offer on T-giving as well as how they end up doing viewership-wise.

The newest Hunger Games movie, Sunrise on the Reaping, had a gigantic opening weekend that exceeded expectations. Some theorized it could struggle as people stayed home to playGTA 6, which released one day prior, but that doesn't appear to have been the case. At the domestic box office, Sunrise on the Reaping earned $120 million for its opening weekend, with $105 million more from international markets for a total of $225 million over its first three days, according to Deadline. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lYXtL5TreOE The franchise's second prequel, after 2023's The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes, Sunrise on the Reaping tells the story of the 50th Hunger Games, where Haymitch Abernathy emerged victorious. Joseph Zada plays him; Woody Harrelson played Haymitch in the original Hunger Games films. Sunrise on the Reaping also stars Ralph Fiennes as a younger President Snow, Jesse Plemons as a younger Plutarch, and Elle Fanning as a younger Effie. With $120 million for its domestic opening, Sunrise on the Reaping is now just the second prequel film ever to start with $100 million or more domestically. The current top prequel is 2016's Star Wars movie Rogue One, which made $155 million for its domestic opening. Some had theorized that Sunrise on the Reaping could suffer as people stayed home to play GTA 6 instead. Director Francis Lawrence stated, "Hopefully, people find time for both." It sure seems like he was right about that. For comparison, The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes debuted to just $44.6 million for its opening weekend in North America, so Sunrise on the Reaping is doing much better. Sunrise on the Reaping is also Lionsgate's biggest post-COVID movie and its first film that opened to $100 million or more since 2015's The Hunger Games: Mockingjay: Part 2 ($102.6 million).

If you're a Sam's Club member, you have access to many early Black Friday deals worth checking out. I spent some time combing through their website and rounded up my favorite tech deals below.

It has been revealed that the Bose SoundLink Flex SE is a portable Bluetooth speaker with an IP67 waterproof rating. The speaker even floats in the water, so you can bring it with you into the pool. While it doesn't offer full EQ customization in its companion app, the sound has rich bass depth and clear highs out of the box. It also features a speakerphone, allowing you to take calls and speak with it. It's light and portable, and the Bluetooth 5.3 supports multipoint connectivity and SBC, AAC, and aptX codecs. You can get the Bose 2nd Generation SoundLink Flex SE for $89 (originally $139).

According to recent reports, skullcandy makes fun speakers and headphones, although they're not designed for audiophiles (their sound signature is very bass-heavy). Their Skullcandy Stomp XL Max is their attempt at making a portable party speaker. It comes with two wireless mics, making it a great option for karaoke. It holds 12 hours of battery life (up to 20 hours with certain settings), has an IPX5 water resistance rating, and has LED lights that sync to the music. You can get it for $99 (originally $199).

Getting a soundbar can exponentially improve anyone's entertainment system, but a 5.1 system with rear speakers and a subwoofer takes it to the next level. The Samsung HW-Q65F 5.1 Channel Soundbar is $299 (originally $399), and it's a wireless setup that will keep the harmony of "too many cables" in the house. It supports Dolby Atmos and DTS Virtual:X to give you a 3D audio feel, and it has a dialogue feature that will let you hear the whispers.

Recent findings suggest that gaming monitors can get expensive swiftly, but you can get decent options on a budget. A great example is the 31.5-inch MSi gaming monitor selling for $129 (originally $179). It has a 250Hz refresh rate and a 1ms response time to make gaming smoother. There's also AMD FreeSync Premium to get rid of tearing and stuttering.

In a recent development, these kinds of sales are always a good time to upgrade laptops. If you're looking for a powerful computer that is well-rounded, consider the 16-inch HP OmniBook 7 Flip going for $699 (originally $899). This laptop comes with an Intel Ultra 5 processor, 512GB of SSD, and 16GB of RAM (which, honestly, is the minimum anyone should be buying in 2026).

It has been revealed that if you need a bigger screen, the 17.3-inch HP OmniBook 3 is a good choice for a bit less money. It comes with an Intel Core Ultra 7 processor, 512GB of SSD, and 12GB of RAM. Part of the bigger screen means a bigger keyboard, so if you deal with numbers a lot, you'd likely appreciate the numeric pad.

If you want your laptop strictly for gaming, the ASUS TUF F16 Gaming laptop is $1,149 (originally $1,399). With an Intel Core 7 processor and the RTX 5060 graphics card, you'll be well set up to tackle heavy games. It comes with a 165Hz refresh rate, Advanced Arc Flow fans and vents to keep your machine cool, and 16GB DDR5 RAM to keep your loads short.

Sources indicate that budget TVs get big discounts during Black Friday, and the 58-inch Vizio QLED TV is one of them. You can get one for $178 (originally $298), and it supports Dolby Vision HDR for better color and contrast. The operating system is the Vizio OS, but of course, you can always change it with a TV dongle if you prefer a different one.

It has been revealed that if you prefer to splurge for a better QLED but still get a good deal, the 65-inch Samsung QN90H QLED TV at $1,197.99 (originally $1,497.99) is a great option. It works for gaming with its 144Hz refresh rate, and because the operating system is Tizen OS, it comes with Samsung TV Plus, which brings over 2,700 free channels. The TV also comes with Dolby Atmos, so you can hear audio with a 3D effect as the audio follows objects around the display.

It has been revealed that A 100-inch TV makes a statement: You take your entertainment system seriously. The 100-inch Vizio QLED TV is a budget-friendly option with a $300 discount, currently going for $1,198 (originally $1,498). This TV supports Dolby Vision HDR for more vivid images and has hundreds of free channels with the Vizio OS.

Recent findings suggest that nowadays, both large retailers and small businesses compete for Black Friday shoppers, so you can expect practically every store to run sales through Monday, November 30, 2026. The “best” sales depend on your needs, but in general, the biggest discounts tend to come from larger retailers who can afford lower prices: think places like Amazon, Walmart, Target, Best Buy, and Home Depot. You can find all the best sales from major retailers on our Black Friday coverage.

Recent findings suggest that black Friday sales officially begin Friday, November 27, 2026, and run throughout “Cyber Week,” the five-day period that runs from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday,  November 30, 2026. But Black Friday and Cyber Monday dates have expanded as retailers compete for customers. You can get the same Black Friday sales early, and we expect sales to wind down by December 2, 2026.

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

She completed her look with a pair of black sunglasses, although that didn’t stop photos showing Belgica in her vibrant ensemble from going viral and sparking conversation online, leading her sister, Grecia, to speak out and set the record straight.

An Instagram post showing the color contrast of Belgica and other attendees read, “Even Miley Cyrus couldn’t get everyone to follow the dress code. Brides, you’re going to be okay 😅.” The clip zoomed in on Belgica as the cheeky message “GUUUUURL” appeared.

In a recent development, “She didn’t know guys, her husband is really good friends with Miley and if you knew my bro in law then you would totally understand,” Grecia replied in the comments section. “My sister should have known better to double check on the invite 😂. Anyway Miley is a sweetheart so she didn’t care as much as the internet does. Our family is having a few laughs.”.

Grecia pointed out that it had been a while since Belgica looked at the invitation, adding, “My sister stated she saw the invite 2 months ago and is gonna go home soon to see the invite and to see where they missed the memo.”.

She also quipped, “Her husband is a colorful guy so we’re surprised he wore black 😂.”.

Grecia later told People that Belgica was admittedly “mortified the first hour,” but luckily no one made the style snafu a bigger deal than it needed to be.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Line of Fire still has a long way to go before the end of its inaugural season — and star Kat Cunning teased why viewers “should be nervous” about what’s to come.

According to recent reports, “You should be nervous because in Line of Fire, you really never know what’s going to happen,” Cunning, 37, exclusively told Us on Tuesday, November 17, while attending Tony Bennett’s 100th Birthday Benefit in Latest York City in celebration of the news about the Tony Bennett Institute for Arts Education. “To be honest, I’m even kept on my toes playing Claire.”.

Cunning, who uses they/them pronouns, has been just as surprised as the audience, adding, “Every episode that I read, I’m on the edge of my seat. But she’s going to go through more when it comes to love and she’s also going to go through a lot more when it comes to her family.”.

Recent findings suggest that line of Fire, which airs Mondays, centers around a family of agents from various branches of law enforcement who find themselves tangled in a deadly conspiracy. In addition to Cunning, the show stars Peter Krause, Hope Davis, Tommy O’Brien, Taylor Bloom and Charlie Barnett.

It has been revealed that “I think the coolest thing about our show is that there’s something that happens every episode — and Claire is often the person solving that mystery,” Cunning told Us. “But also, the long arc of what’s going on with her family is like right now in filming.”.

Cunning promised the show is “finally starting to unfold the most dramatic underbelly of the mystery.”.

Sources indicate that “I am so excited to be learning about her every day. All I can say is keep tuning in because it’s not a one-episode thing,” they continued. “Literally today at work, I was like, ‘You guys, what’s going to happen?’ It continues to surprise us and I love playing Claire because she gets to be somebody who’s like on the case and solving things like the strong woman that she is. But she also gets to have emotions and be bratty and have love surprise her. A lot is coming.”.

While NBC’s newest show’s first season is not even halfway finished, Cunning already has ideas for season 2. More specifically, Cunning is hoping their partner Jules Latimer will make a cameo — or they could make an appearance on Latimer’s Fire Country.

“I would love a crossover. I’m trying to be a hot ranch girl in Fire Country. Write me in. And Jules, we’re already pitching [a cameo on Line of Fire],” Cunning told Us. “Don’t you think she could be the chef in the White House or something? I feel like we should absolutely be cross pollinating. In general, I am manifesting a chance to work with my fiancée because I think the world of her as an actor and we haven’t ever done it yet.”.

They concluded, “But we’re both tuning into each other’s shows and it’s a crazy thing to be queer characters on network TV in 2026.”.

Industry observers note that cunning took a break from set to support Tony Bennett’s 100th Birthday Benefit. During the event, it was announced that Tony’s legacy of love, gratitude and spreading the gift of music would be highlighted with Exploring the Arts (ETA) and Third Street Music School planning to open the Tony Bennett Institute for Arts Education at Third Street (TBIAE).

“‘The Way You Look Tonight’ is one of the songs that made me learn how to sing,” Cunning told Us. “I’m a deep alto and I’ve learned other parts of my voice, But as a singer, those jazz songs are the things that give me my entry point because they’re all style and all swag and no belting — at least at first. So I fell in love with that song.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that “Cancer does change you,” Kate Middleton indicates, emotion clear in her voice. “It changes your body, it changes you physically. But there’s a much, much deeper part to what a cancer diagnosis shifts in you.” These words come not at as an Instagram post or at a public event. Instead, they're the voice-over in a previously unannounced documentary about the Princess of Wales and her life since she disclosed a diagnosis of cancer in 2024.

According to Kensington Palace, which confirmed the film on Saturday, Heal is “a deeply personal upcoming documentary from The Princess of Wales, exploring life beyond diagnosis and the many ways people find comfort, strength and hope in the face of serious illness.” It will air on the BBC in the UK on November 29, and in the US on NBCUniversal on November 30.

It has been revealed that heal follows Kate Middleton during her participation in one of the United Kingdom’s most demanding endurance events: The National Three Peaks Challenge, which she completed this summer. In less than 24 hours, the princess climbed the three highest mountains in Scotland, England, and Wales: Ben Nevis (4,413 feet), Scafell Pike (3,209 feet), and Yr Wyddfa–Snowdon (3,559 feet). The undertaking wasn't just a personal effort, as it was also in support of the Royal Marsden Cancer Charity, an organization that supports people living with cancer before, during, and after the disease.

The documentary will also support that organization, Kensington Palace notes, saying “All funds received through the documentary's distribution have been directed to The Royal Marsden Cancer Charity to help people living with and beyond cancer.” The Royal Marsden Hospital, at which Middleton received treatment, is also referenced in the film, as Middleton's brother, James, asks her “Isn’t it when you leave the Royal Marsden, you ring the bell?”.

But while many patients participate in the bell-ringing ritual at the conclusion of treatment, Middleton states she missed out on that moment. “Yeah, but I didn’t ring the bell,” she replies. “So maybe this is your ringing of the bell,” James responded, suggesting her Three Peaks experience was that symbolic peal.

While Prince William is no stranger to documentary work, nor are Prince Harry and wife Meghan Markle, this is Kate Middleton's first venture into the format. Perhaps to ease her into the project, Heal's Director of Photography is a face quite familiar to the Princess: Will Warr, the filmmaker behind her video announcement marking the end of her chemotherapy treatments.

According to recent reports, “Through this documentary, The Princess hopes to help others navigate diagnosis, recovery and life beyond cancer and transform access to holistic cancer care which supports wellbeing, resilience and quality of life during and after diagnosis,” Kensington Palace indicates of Heal, a message underscored by Middleton's words in the trailer. “You know, healing is a journey. How to reconnect with the things you once knew and how to find a sense of hope and joy alongside uncertainty.”.

Industry observers note that “It’s clear we're not meant to face life’s challenges alone,” the princess says as the trailer concludes. “Things can renew and grow. Often it is through pain that we realize that there is a greater beauty that lies beyond that.".

Grand Theft Auto 6 has plenty of fun Easter eggs--many of which tie back to earlier games in the series--but you can also find a few nods to other megapopular game franchises hiding within the vast map of Leonida. If you take a detour along the north side of Lummox County, you'll come across an area in the woods that looks like it'd be right at home in a Super Mario Bros. game, and you can even collect two distinct caps for your troubles--which might suggest that the greater Mario multiverse theory is true after all. How to find the GTA 6 Super Mario Bros. Easter egg in GTA 6 You can mark this location on your map, as you can find the reference to the Nintendo mascot in Lummox County. It's up north from Mount Kalaga, at the end of a twisty road that seemingly goes nowhere: Hit the bong, dude Once you've arrived, scout the area for a purple tarp that has a bong sitting on it. Smoke it, get high, and climb the structure in front of you. You'll notice that there's a plume of smoke coming out of the one column, and if you stand in it, an invisible block will appear above your head. Smash the block Jump up, and you'll smash the block. You won't get any gold coins for your trouble, but you will get a nostalgic tune and two caps that reference Nintendo's favorite plumbers, Mario and Luigi. Collect the caps Each cap has an initial embroidered on it: "J" for Jason, "L" for Lucia. You can add them to your collection, or leave them to gather dust; it's up to you. As mentioned above, GTA 6 has references to a lot of pop culture. Someone at Rockstar Games is clearly a huge Dexter fan, Bigfoot is on the prowl, and I really wish I'd chosen the elevator without a killer clown inside it. For everything else on the biggest game of the year--and maybe even the decade--check out GameSpot's GTA 6 guides hub.

Industry observers note that you can mark this location on your map, as you can find the reference to the Nintendo mascot in Lummox County. It's up north from Mount Kalaga, at the end of a twisty road that seemingly goes nowhere:.

Once you've arrived, scout the area for a purple tarp that has a bong sitting on it. Smoke it, get high, and climb the structure in front of you. You'll notice that there's a plume of smoke coming out of the one column, and if you stand in it, an invisible block will appear above your head.

Jump up, and you'll smash the block. You won't get any gold coins for your trouble, but you will get a nostalgic tune and two caps that reference Nintendo's favorite plumbers, Mario and Luigi.

According to recent reports, each cap has an initial embroidered on it: "J" for Jason, "L" for Lucia. You can add them to your collection, or leave them to gather dust; it's up to you.

As mentioned above, GTA 6 has references to a lot of pop culture. Someone at Rockstar Games is clearly a huge Dexter fan, Bigfoot is on the prowl, and I really wish I'd chosen the elevator without a killer clown inside it. For everything else on the biggest game of the year--and maybe even the decade--check out GameSpot's GTA 6 guides hub.

Gabriel “Fluffy” Iglesias‘ spokesperson is addressing the comedian’s condition after he fell ill and had to be helped off stage during a Raleigh, North Carolina, show.

“Gabe is doing much better today,” his rep told Us on Monday, November 23.

Hours earlier, a viral video circulated via social media, showing alarming scenes at the comic’s Sunday, November 22, performance at the Lenovo Center. Iglesias could be seen hunched over a stool on stage, calling for opener Martin Moreno to help him away. (TMZ was the first to report the news.).

An edit in the clip cut to Iglesias, 50, receiving oxygen just off stage moments later as Moreno, 58, closed the show by explaining that the headline act wasn’t feeling well. Iglesias had earlier mentioned near the beginning of his set that he was under the weather.

“[Gabriel] has been sick the last week or so,” the spokesperson confirmed to Us. “He didn’t want to cancel on his fans, so he tried to pull through to give them a great show.”.

Iglesias nor Moreno have yet to personally address the incident from Sunday’s live show.

Fellow comedian Dane Cook publicly reached out to Iglesias via Instagram on Monday, revealing that he’d heard about the concerning viral video while offering his fellow comedian his support.

It has been revealed that “Just heard the news about Gabriel Iglesias,” Cook, 54, said in an Instagram Reel. “Fluffy, we love you. I hope everything’s OK. Please, everybody, send nothing but positive thoughts and prayers.”.

Cook encouraged his longtime friend to take the necessary time to recover once he is feeling better.

In a recent development, “Gabriel Iglesias is one of the good guys,” Cook added. “This dude just sold out SoFi Stadium. He took standup comedy to unbelievable heights, and we want him around for a long time. Fluffy, get better, and then take a vacation! OK? I’ll go with you. And I don’t even like to vacation either, but we’ll go together. Cook and Fluffy, the Do Nothing Tour — on a beach!”.

As Cook mentioned, Iglesias achieved a rare feat for a standup comic by selling out SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California, alongside fellow comedian Jo Koy for a special “One Night Only” event in March.

He is scheduled to perform next at the FedEx Forum in Memphis on Saturday, November 28, before wrapping up his 2026 live dates in Melbourne, Australia, at the Rod Laver Arena on Saturday, December 12.

The comic is scheduled to hit the road for more 1976 Tour: A Fluffy Celebration gigs in the Latest Year, starting with four nights at El Paso’s Plaza Theater from Thursday, January 7, 2027 through Sunday, January 10, 2027.

It has been revealed that iglesias has been performing live comedy since 1997, having parlayed his stage success to supporting roles in the Magic Mike movies and his own Netflix sitcom, Mr. Iglesias. #165880. Why Do AI Posters All Look Like That?

AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

Why Do AI Posters All Look Like That?

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1296 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that you know “the look” by now.
  • At this point, gone are the days of chatbots like ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini simply generating text immediately in response to a prompt.
  • To borrow a classic and implausible example, if you were to give an AI chatbot the instruction “Make a peanut butter and jelly sandwich,” it would start by generating step-by-step instructions on how to make the sandwich before trying to make one (if it could).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that you know “the look” by now. Every poster for a business or event has pictures of uncanny-looking people, buildings that don’t look right, and always that one font. But why? If generative AI is supposedly able to “think” and be “creative,” why do so many of its results come out looking exactly the same? The answer is complicated, and it has to do with what chatbots define as “thinking.”.

At this point, gone are the days of chatbots like ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini simply generating text immediately in response to a prompt. Some very fast models do, but most employ what’s known as “thinking models”, which are a bit of a misnomer. The “thinking” really just consists of generating a set of sub-prompts before executing the main one. And it’s in that hidden, generated text that most of the “choices” (to the extent that we can call the statistical output of an AI model a “choice”) occur that determine how a design looks.

To borrow a classic and implausible example, if you were to give an AI chatbot the instruction “Make a peanut butter and jelly sandwich,” it would start by generating step-by-step instructions on how to make the sandwich before trying to make one (if it could). Most of this happens invisibly in the background, and many proprietary chatbots won’t show you their in-process “thinking” prompts even if you ask.

In the case of an AI poster, it might break down “make a poster” into smaller steps such as “create a design brief for a poster.” To demonstrate this while doing some testing for this piece, I added additional prompts for ChatGPT to explain the “design briefs” it generated, which included details like layout, colors, and typography.

The problem is those instructions are still subject to the same flaws as any other AI-generated text. They can’t properly fact-check; they can’t walk into the real world and see the thing they’re describing; and they can hallucinate or fall back on stale formats that become easy to notice after a while.

For example, while testing, I had ChatGPT generate a poster for a Lifehacker-themed nightclub. In every case, the underlying brief it generated outlined some basic details, but occasionally it added things I hadn’t asked for. This included additional text, iconography, and in one case it even added the “design brief” explanation I had requested as the bottom half of the poster.

Sources indicate that those mistakes filter into the final product, when the brief is then fed into the image generator that ultimately makes the poster. In my case, ChatGPT revealed me the underlying explanations for its reasoning (though even that could be different from what was actually sent to the image generator), but most people who use a chatbot for this task won’t see these factors before getting the final result.

It has been revealed that while most chatbots won’t show you exactly what underlying “thinking” they use, most can be coaxed into describing the vague outlines of how they reached certain outcomes. And those descriptions provide some insight into why certain chatbots keep outputting similar results over and over. It doesn’t take long for some patterns to emerge. For example, any prompt to generate a poster for a nightclub almost invariably generated a brief that had specifications for a color palette including “electric purple,” “electric yellow,” and “electric pink.”.

Industry observers note that the reason for this should be pretty obvious: When the statistical model underlying LLMs needs to come up with an example for “colors for a nightclub poster,” the most obvious answers are neon, high-energy colors. Unless you know something about the specific club’s vibe (and write that out and feed it to the chatbot), the AI will have to fill in the gaps with something. And that something will be based on the same statistics it uses to predict any word.

According to recent reports, this pattern of repetition was everywhere in all the design rationale ChatGPT gave me. Across multiple attempts to generate a Club Lifehacker poster, the generated design brief added an overarching “concept” that described the fictional club’s atmosphere as “high-energy” and “futuristic.” Every bot mentioned using images with the “silhouette” of either the DJ or a dancing crowd (often both). All the text had to be “bold” and “futuristic.".

Sources indicate that if there's one dead giveaway that a poster was made with AI, it's that one brush-stroke font that they all seem to use. Now, this is a bit more speculative, but I have a theory on where that specific design comes from. And it’s worth noting upfront that this seems to only apply to posters generated by ChatGPT specifically.

In a recent development, one of the most common factors I found in my design brief testing was the use of phrases like “brush lettering” or “brush script.” Brush lettering is a design term that refers to using any number of methods like markers, paint brushes, or brush pens to write text. In digital design, that can take the form of fonts that are designed to emulate the look of fancy, handwritten text.

In every test poster I created, however, ChatGPT seemed to take the phrase “brush lettering” rather literally. Every instance I encountered of a design brief that mentioned any kind of “brush” text generated an image with letters that looked as though they were created with a broad paint brush. A human designer would understand “brush lettering” to mean “something that looks handwritten," but ChatGPT didn’t seem capable of understanding the phrase as anything other than using an actual paint brush.

Sources indicate that the generated posters aren’t even using a “font,” strictly speaking. (Often, letters that should be identical had slight variations.) The image generator part of the chatbot is still a diffusion model, so it can’t employ a vector-based font, per se. But the brush-style font is so common that its look surfaces in any statistical model.

According to recent reports, this is an odd quirk of ChatGPT specifically, and it’s possible that it could change in the future. Especially if OpenAI intentionally tries to train this behavior out of its chatbot. However, it’s helpful to illustrate the underlying mechanism. The only way a chatbot can conceptualize design elements in a visual medium is to generate more specific text to feed to the image generator. And that text is just as prone to mistakes and blandness as any other AI model.

Sources indicate that I’ve been examining this with a focus on the kinds of posters ChatGPT generates because they’re very common, but posters (or any AI-generated content) from other models might look different. Every model has its own tendencies. For example, a lot of vibecoded websites are made with Anthropic’s Claude, and you can often tell by the tiny text, buttons with rounded corners, and tile-based layouts.

It has been revealed that to a certain extent, this is inevitable. While AI models are very different from humans and do not make “choices” in the same way people do, design elements still have to come from somewhere, and whether human or AI, it’s impossible to make these decisions in a vacuum. Humans will have preferences based on the things they like or emotionally resonate with, and AI models will have tendencies based on what their statistical model determines is the most appropriate output.

That means that an AI model’s “style” is naturally going to change over time. Even if a model improves or makes fewer mistakes, it’s impossible to ever change the fact that all ChatGPT images are made by ChatGPT. Whatever you generate with any particular model will have a lot in common with what everyone else who uses the same tool generates.

GTA 6: All The Secret Controls And Gameplay Features You Might Have Missed

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 14 min read (2895 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamespot

⏱️ ~14 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that on the surface, Grand Theft Auto 6 has a pretty standard control scheme for its protagonists.
  • According to recent reports, on the surface, Grand Theft Auto 6 has a pretty standard control scheme for its protagonists.
  • It has been revealed that instead, you're left to discover them as you play, and each one adds another layer of immersion to the experience.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that on the surface, Grand Theft Auto 6 has a pretty standard control scheme for its protagonists. You've got everything you'd expect for exploring its open-world environment, from options to sprint to aiming your gun, but there's a whole lot more to the game when you start experimenting with the inputs. Whether you're driving or jogging, Jason and Lucia are capable of a whole lot more, and these hidden features aren't thrown at you when you start the game. Instead, you're left to discover them as you play, and each one adds another layer of immersion to the experience. If you don't want to accidentally stumble on them, here's a closer look at every hidden gameplay feature we've discovered so far. For more on GTA 6, from completing side missions to finding a tricky location on the sprawling map of Leonida, we’ve got you covered with our Grand Theft Auto 6 guides hub. Go into first-person mode Want to examine the world in more detail around you? Press L2 (LT on Xbox) to highlight something, then press R3 to go into first-person mode. Ordinarily, you can't move around in this mode, but there is a glitch to force the game to lock you into first-person. Change shoulder cameras Not too massive a fan of the default over-the-shoulder aiming in GTA 6? You can switch which shoulder you aim from during combat by holding the left button on your D-pad while aiming with L2. Quick-swap between weapons At the same time, you can also quick-swap between weapons by tapping Triangle/Y while aiming, allowing you to keep blastin' like you're some sort of Frank Reynolds character. Do a combat roll! Need to close the gap quickly and avoid taking a few lead injections? Tap X/A while aiming, and you'll do a combat roll. Do a backflip! To show off some athleticism, run towards water, and as you get to the edge, hold X/A on the controller to do a backflip. Pistol-whip when you're out of bullets Got a gun in your hand, but you're out of bullets? It turns out that firearms are still good for inflicting blunt-force trauma, as you can use the melee attack (Square on PS5, X on Xbox) to knock enemies out. Choke enemies out For a stealthy beatdown, start a fight in GTA 6, grapple your opponent with R2, and then hold Square/X to set them up for a chokehold. Press the indicated D-pad button on your controller, and you'll trigger the chokehold. Chain-jump across gaps If you're running across an area that has multiple small gaps, you can tap X to jump across and tap it again to keep your momentum going. Your car door is also a weapon Instead of damaging the hood of your car in GTA 6, put a dent in your door by smashing it into a pedestrian. Like melee attacks, you can hit Square/X on your controller while driving to nail an unlucky person with the door. Your feet are technically free when you're on a bike And if you're not in a car? You can relive your Road Rash days by hitting the melee button to kick someone instead while you scoot around on a bike. Change how you wear your cap Whether you like to wear your cap in a traditional sun-blocking style or backwards, you can swap the position of your headwear easily. Just open the items and weapon wheel by holding L1, select items, and navigate to your cap. Press X/A and you can switch styles. Distract enemies with some whistling, which I can't do in real life GTA 6 makes for a surprisingly good stealth game, and for those scenarios where you need to draw enemy attention, you can whistle at them. Crouch, take cover, hold L2 to aim at a target, and press Triangle/Y to whistle. Loiter like a champ with leaning actions One of the cooler features in GTA 6 for photography fans is the option to lean against walls and railings. When you're near a wall, you can hold Circle/B to lean against it, and when next to a railing, press L3 to rest on that structure--pretty cool for when you want to take a photograph of Jason or Lucia while they chill out. If you're on solid ground, you can also hold down Circle/B to sit down. Choose your favorite hand If you want Jason or Lucia to emulate your dominant hand while they're holding something, press left or right on the D-pad. You can also make them hold two items at the same time, in case you want to show off that you're one of the lucky even-handed few. Auto-drive to destinations  One of our favorite modes in the game--especially when we want to soak in the scenery of Vice City--auto-drive is pretty easy to miss. While you're driving, hold the down button on the D-pad, press Start to enable Cinematic Mode, and then hold Circle/B to switch to auto-drive mode. You can also set the speed between slow/normal/fast for your commute. Quick-scan vehicles Instead of navigating to your WAiNK app, just hold Up on your D-Pad to bring it up instantly. Duck while driving so you can avoid being shot You're going to be in plenty of high-speed shootouts in GTA 6, and if you want to keep your head on your shoulders, hold the Circle/B button while driving to duck down. You have turn signals; use them Unless you're driving the equivalent of a BMW in GTA 6, you should use turn signals. While you're in your car, tap left or right on your D-pad to use these lights. They'll also cancel automatically after you've made a turn. Switch car headlights on and off Want to drive in stealth mode at night? Tap the circle button to turn off your headlights. Just don't be too surprised if other motorists flash you with their lights to remind you that you're driving dark. Leave the engine running Want to prepare your vehicle to be in getaway mode for a heist that you're about to pull off? You can leave the engine running by double-tapping Triangle/Y as you exit your car. Just be aware that this could invite car thieves to swipe your vehicle, since you're leaving it out there and purring. If you do this while piloting a boat, it'll also sail on while you explore the deck. Push vehicles In case you're stuck in a ditch or out of fuel, you can push your vehicle to safety. Position yourself behind, next to, or in front of your car (or boat), and keep pushing your character into it with the left stick until they switch to a pushing animation. Hold Square/X to move the vehicle, or flip it in case it has been overturned or beached. Leave your car door open You can also shave valuable seconds off your getaway by keeping your car door open. As you exit your car, press triangle once. Slide across your car hood For some Dukes of Hazzard action, sprint towards your car, aim for the hood, and tap X to slide across it. Yeehaw. Drop anchor If you don't want your boat to sail away without you while you search the ocean depths for treasure, make certain that you drop anchor. Press and hold left on the D-pad while piloting a boat, navigate to the vehicle menu with the right analog stick, and choose Anchor to lower it. Additional vehicle controls On that note, you can also find extra vehicle controls by bringing up the radio menu (press and hold left on the D-pad), and using the right analogue stick to navigate up. Turn radios on and off instantly If you're anything like me and your ears start to bleed when you boost a car that has the country music station turned on, double-tap left on the D-pad to instantly switch it off. You can smoke while driving Not that you should because it's bad for your health and both hands should be on the steering wheel, but you can hold L1 to bring up your items wheel, select cigarettes or a cigar, and then select R1 or R2 to start puffing away. Flick a cigarette You can also flick your cigarette when you're done smoking by holding the R2 button. Aim, and do that after you've poured out a trail of fuel on the ground, for extra cinema-style points. Flip the bird while driving The universal hand sign for telling someone that their driving is not up to par can easily be done by aiming at a motorist with L2 and then pressing R1 on your controller. Trash talk drivers Or if you need to give some verbal abuse, pull up next to another driver, press L2 to aim at them, and press R3 to give them some grief. Just don't be too surprised if they respond violently to your provocations.

Got a gun in your hand, but you're out of bullets? It turns out that firearms are still good for inflicting blunt-force trauma, as you can use the melee attack (Square on PS5, X on Xbox) to knock enemies out.

For a stealthy beatdown, start a fight in GTA 6, grapple your opponent with R2, and then hold Square/X to set them up for a chokehold. Press the indicated D-pad button on your controller, and you'll trigger the chokehold.

If you're running across an area that has multiple small gaps, you can tap X to jump across and tap it again to keep your momentum going.

Instead of damaging the hood of your car in GTA 6, put a dent in your door by smashing it into a pedestrian. Like melee attacks, you can hit Square/X on your controller while driving to nail an unlucky person with the door.

And if you're not in a car? You can relive your Road Rash days by hitting the melee button to kick someone instead while you scoot around on a bike.

Recent findings suggest that whether you like to wear your cap in a traditional sun-blocking style or backwards, you can swap the position of your headwear easily. Just open the items and weapon wheel by holding L1, select items, and navigate to your cap. Press X/A and you can switch styles.

According to recent reports, GTA 6 makes for a surprisingly good stealth game, and for those scenarios where you need to draw enemy attention, you can whistle at them. Crouch, take cover, hold L2 to aim at a target, and press Triangle/Y to whistle.

Recent findings suggest that one of the cooler features in GTA 6 for photography fans is the option to lean against walls and railings. When you're near a wall, you can hold Circle/B to lean against it, and when next to a railing, press L3 to rest on that structure--pretty cool for when you want to take a photograph of Jason or Lucia while they chill out. If you're on solid ground, you can also hold down Circle/B to sit down.

In a recent development, if you want Jason or Lucia to emulate your dominant hand while they're holding something, press left or right on the D-pad. You can also make them hold two items at the same time, in case you want to show off that you're one of the lucky even-handed few.

One of our favorite modes in the game--especially when we want to soak in the scenery of Vice City--auto-drive is pretty easy to miss. While you're driving, hold the down button on the D-pad, press Start to enable Cinematic Mode, and then hold Circle/B to switch to auto-drive mode. You can also set the speed between slow/normal/fast for your commute.

Instead of navigating to your WAiNK app, just hold Up on your D-Pad to bring it up instantly.

You're going to be in plenty of high-speed shootouts in GTA 6, and if you want to keep your head on your shoulders, hold the Circle/B button while driving to duck down.

Sources indicate that unless you're driving the equivalent of a BMW in GTA 6, you should use turn signals. While you're in your car, tap left or right on your D-pad to use these lights. They'll also cancel automatically after you've made a turn.

Want to drive in stealth mode at night? Tap the circle button to turn off your headlights. Just don't be too surprised if other motorists flash you with their lights to remind you that you're driving dark.

In a recent development, want to prepare your vehicle to be in getaway mode for a heist that you're about to pull off? You can leave the engine running by double-tapping Triangle/Y as you exit your car. Just be aware that this could invite car thieves to swipe your vehicle, since you're leaving it out there and purring. If you do this while piloting a boat, it'll also sail on while you explore the deck.

In a recent development, in case you're stuck in a ditch or out of fuel, you can push your vehicle to safety. Position yourself behind, next to, or in front of your car (or boat), and keep pushing your character into it with the left stick until they switch to a pushing animation. Hold Square/X to move the vehicle, or flip it in case it has been overturned or beached.

Industry observers note that you can also shave valuable seconds off your getaway by keeping your car door open. As you exit your car, press triangle once.

For some Dukes of Hazzard action, sprint towards your car, aim for the hood, and tap X to slide across it. Yeehaw.

In a recent development, if you don't want your boat to sail away without you while you search the ocean depths for treasure, make certain that you drop anchor. Press and hold left on the D-pad while piloting a boat, navigate to the vehicle menu with the right analog stick, and choose Anchor to lower it.

On that note, you can also find extra vehicle controls by bringing up the radio menu (press and hold left on the D-pad), and using the right analogue stick to navigate up.

If you're anything like me and your ears start to bleed when you boost a car that has the country music station turned on, double-tap left on the D-pad to instantly switch it off.

Not that you should because it's bad for your health and both hands should be on the steering wheel, but you can hold L1 to bring up your items wheel, select cigarettes or a cigar, and then select R1 or R2 to start puffing away.

You can also flick your cigarette when you're done smoking by holding the R2 button. Aim, and do that after you've poured out a trail of fuel on the ground, for extra cinema-style points.

The universal hand sign for telling someone that their driving is not up to par can easily be done by aiming at a motorist with L2 and then pressing R1 on your controller.

Recent findings suggest that or if you need to give some verbal abuse, pull up next to another driver, press L2 to aim at them, and press R3 to give them some grief. Just don't be too surprised if they respond violently to your provocations.

Kim Zolciak isn’t letting her family’s legal challenges distract from daughter Brielle Biermann’s romantic Florida wedding.

“It was perfect,” Zolciak, 48, told paparazzi of her daughter’s recent nuptials on Sunday, November 22, while walking through the Southwest Florida International Airport in Fort Myers, Florida, according to footage published by Page Six.

The Real Housewives of Atlanta alum described her daughter’s special day as “beautiful,” confirming “of course” she gave a toast and it was “great.”.

“It was all a dream,” Zolciak gushed as she traveled through the airport alongside boyfriend Kyle Mowitz and son Kash Biermann following the Saturday, November 21, ceremony.

When asked whether anything was “missing” amid her estranged husband Kroy Biermann’s absence at the celebratory event, Zolciak rapidly responded, “No.”.

In a recent development, zolciak and Kroy, 41, are at the moment tied up in a messy divorce after splitting in 2023. The exes share four children and Kroy is the adoptive stepfather to her two eldest daughters, Brielle, 29, and Ariana Biermann.

Zolciak appeared calm on Sunday as she headed toward security, wearing a yellow shirt and matching yellow sweatpants and sneakers.

She didn’t, however, address her and Kroy’s son KJ Biermann’s absence from the wedding amid his sexual assault and sodomy arrest.

KJ, 15, was arrested in August for alleged aggravated sodomy and aggravated sexual assault, per court records obtained by Us.

Both Zolciak and KJ’s attorney have denied the allegations, claiming they are “false.” He is right now fighting the seven charges outlined in his indictment.

Despite the shadow KJ’s arrest has cast on Zolciak and her loved ones, the family was in town for Zolciak’s eldest child’s wedding on Saturday when Brielle married baseball player Billy Seidl in Naples, Florida.

The bride wore a traditional white, flowy wedding dress with a large black bow on the left side, while Seidl, 27, chose a tuxedo and black bowtie for the occasion.

Industry observers note that zolciak brought Mowitz as her plus one to the event, where she celebrated Brielle alongside most of her children. Daughter Ariana, 25, served as Brielle’s maid of honor, while Kash, 14, was spotted at the airport with his mom.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, this week's column is bleak.
  • According to recent reports, you can judge a generation by the illegal drugs it pioneers.
  • Would-be muscle-men have been injecting themselves with black market ‘rhoids since the Eisenhower administration, but that was a small cult of adult weirdos with a specific goal.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, this week's column is bleak. First, there's the looksmaxxing trend where teenagers are taking dangerous chemicals to correct perceived physical shortcomings. Then there are the AI job interviewers. Depressing, but at least some young people are having a little fun with their dystopian hellscape.

According to recent reports, you can judge a generation by the illegal drugs it pioneers. In the 1960s, hippies smoked weed and dropped acid to expand their consciousness; the yuppies of the go-go '80s fueled their drive to acquire with Colombian cocaine; but kids today don’t want to go deeper or work harder. They have a smaller, sadder goal: They take drugs to look better. The substance of choice for a growing number of teenage boys are steroids, peptides, and other exotic chemicals designed to enhance appearance.

Would-be muscle-men have been injecting themselves with black market ‘rhoids since the Eisenhower administration, but that was a small cult of adult weirdos with a specific goal. In 2026, kids are into it, and they aren’t using steroids to win a $500 prize in the Mr. Topeka contest; they’re using unapproved research chemicals to looksmaxx. Looksmaxxing is an online movement of young men trying to maximize their physical appearance. Teenagers are taking the normal desire to look their best to dangerous, pathological levels. Driven by a combination of undiagnosed body dysmorphia and relentless social media algorithms that turn amoral “red pill” kooks into gurus, teenage boys are ingesting a panoply of exotic and dangerous compounds in a quest to fix the angle of their jawlines, change their skin tone, lose weight, grow taller, and otherwise “correct” perceived physical problems.

It has been revealed that in the "good old days" of steroid abuse, people generally stuck to abusing anabolic-androgenic steroids that had at least been tested for decades. Teens today are buying SARMs (Selective Androgen Receptor Modulators) and synthetic peptides marked "not for human consumption" from shady laboratories online. Steroids primarily affect the muscles, but many of these newer substances target different biological systems. A recent Rolling Stone article reports that kids are “heightmaxxing” by swallowing erdafitinib, a drug that treats advanced urothelial cancer, because the drug is known to trigger growth spurts (that can result in a curvature of the spine and other nasty side effects). They’re also trying MK-677 to get taller, an experimental growth hormone secretagogue that carries the risk of insulin resistance, water retention, and high blood pressure. Others are injecting Melanotan II, a synthetic peptide that forces a long-lasting deep tan, with side effects of extreme nausea and the sudden, aggressive darkening of moles. (And they're doing steroids too.).

In the looksmaxxing community, softmaxxing is doing generally-considered-acceptable things to look better, like getting enough sleep, exercising regularly, and eating a balanced diet. Hardmaxxing is taking more extreme measures like plastic surgery, smashing your face with a hammer, or taking experimental drugs.

In the bodybuilding and looksmaxxing community, “natty” refers to a natural, non-steroid-enhanced physique.

It has been revealed that here's something more lighthearted than the growing popularity of illicit self-esteem chemicals: the bicep heart and waist heart trends. The Bicep heart came first. Thirst trap videos started appearing on Instagram and TikTok in October in which dudes make a heart with their hand and bicep. Then people started posting variations where they frame the shot with someone they love inside the heart. The bicep heart quickly led to women posting the waist heart.

Industry observers note that okay. So maybe it's not that lighthearted of a trend. While there are some videos of dudes with skinny arms doing the bicep heart, it's mostly jacked dudes. And the waist heart doesn't seem like it would work at all unless you are a specific shape, as this video illustrates. So maybe this isn't a silly meme but an illustration of how young people are inundated with content that can trigger feelings of physical unworthiness, even if they're just looking for silly memes.

It has been revealed that as if searching for a job wasn't alienating and horrible enough, some companies have begun using AI agents to conduct interviews. Begging a robot to let you work in a cubicle farm is as dystopian as anything Phillip K. Dick ever imagined, but don't count humanity out yet. Young people are sticking a finger in the eye of the machine by creating comedy videos that focus on trolling these AI job interviewers. They're hilarious because AI is the ultimate straight person in a comedy team, and the raw compute costs to run these interviews means corporate money is burning with each second of wasted time. Here are some of the top creators in the genre.

Bo Bongo: This YouTuber indicates up to AI interviews shirtless but insists he's wearing a "corporate tube top," then focuses on daring the interviewer to notice he's doing things like smoking a cigarette or eating a rotisserie chicken.

Cam Whitt likes to wind up AI by arguing, interrupting, telling outrageous lies, and asking the dumbest questions imaginable, like, "When does the interview actually start?" and "How do I figure out what my name is?".

Grahamn Raabe: Among this YouTuber's schticks is speaking only in nonsense, like describing his professional background as "freight cadence, walnut, a little bit of Richard, spruce wood—six years of spruce wood.".

According to recent reports, nick Reid: Is so obnoxious, he seems to make the AI furious at him, even though it's a computer without emotions. Two thumbs up!

Two Of My Favorite Hallmark Actors Are Finally In A Movie Together And I’m Obsessed

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (686 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cinemablend

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Hallmark churns out nearly a hundred new romance movies every year.
  • After spending 20 years with the cable channel and being friends for 18 years, Cahill and Walker finally got to share the screen as romantic leads in Christmas in Blue Dog Valley.
  • The residents of Blue Dog Valley aren’t too thrilled about an outsider taking over their beloved veterinary practice, and Goldie has to work overtime to win over the hearts of the town’s loyal pet owners.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hallmark churns out nearly a hundred new romance movies every year. The 2026 Countdown to Christmas lineup alone is slated for 34 original holiday-themed flicks. Part of the reason it’s easy for the cable channel-turned-streamer to make so many movies a year is that it has a list of dedicated actors who are eager to star in these films -- like Queen of Hallmark Lacey Chabert. And yet, somehow, they manage to keep the pairings fresh. So fresh that two of my favorite longtime Hallmark actors, Erin Cahill and Andrew Walker, just starred in their first movie together. I’m happy to report it was worth the wait!

Yep, you read that right. After spending 20 years with the cable channel and being friends for 18 years, Cahill and Walker finally got to share the screen as romantic leads in Christmas in Blue Dog Valley. The holiday flick follows Goldie MacKenzie (Cahil), a former Hollywood on-set veterinarian, who decides to leave the glitz and glamour for a slower life as the in-house veterinarian in the small town of Blue Dog Valley.

The residents of Blue Dog Valley aren’t too thrilled about an outsider taking over their beloved veterinary practice, and Goldie has to work overtime to win over the hearts of the town’s loyal pet owners. Desperate for an ally, Goldie turns to Cohen (Walker), the son of the former owner of the vet practice, for help. While they get off to a rough start, sparks start to fly as the two spend more time together, especially with Goldie taking over planning duties for the annual Christmas parade that will feature the four-legged and furry residents of the town this year.

It’s not just their characters who have love for each other, though. Both Cahill and Walker have a deep appreciation for each other and their decades-long friendship. In talking with Hallmark on set, both of these iconic stars shared how excited they were to be sharing the screen together for the first time. Take a look:.

A post shared by Hallmark Channel (@hallmarkchannel).

It has been revealed that it can be easy for the human actors to get upstaged by their animal co-stars, especially when there are so many different types of animals in a movie (cows, alpacas, and of course dogs in this case), but Cahill and Walker managed to hold things down even in the face of an adorable, overweight corgi. It’s a testament to the chemistry these two have on screen.

Their characters don’t share as much time on screen together as some of the other couples in Hallmark’s Christmas movies. However, the time they are together is swoonworthy — well, once they got over their meet-cute, that is. I definitely wouldn’t mind a sequel revisiting Goldie and Cohen a year from now. Or, better yet, I’d love to see Cahill and Walker star in even more Hallmark movies together now that it’s clear that they play compelling and entertaining romantic leads.

Recent findings suggest that blue Dog Valley might not be my favorite Hallmark Christmas movie of 2026, but it's still worth the watch. If you missed the live airing, you can stream it now with an active Hallmark+ subscription. While there, check out my favorite Cahill movie, Christmas on Cherry Lane, or my favorite Walker film, Three Wise Men and a Baby.
